items.body:
FORT HOOD, Texas – An Army sergeant caught on a Ring camera striking a young child pleaded guilty to domestic violence during his court-martial Oct. 7 at the Lawrence Williams Judicial Center.

Sgt. Paul A. Thames, an automated logistics specialist assigned to the 9th Cavalry Regiment, 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, was sentenced by the military judge to one year in prison and a bad conduct discharge from the Army. The judge gave him 181 days of confinement credit for time served prior to his trial.

On the evening of Jan. 16, 2026, Thames was babysitting his girlfriend’s 3-year-old son at her apartment in Waco, Texas, when he was caught by a neighbor’s Ring doorbell camera punching the boy multiple times, then picking him up by the head and neck.

The neighbor immediately notified the Waco Police Department and officers responded to the scene, taking Thames into custody.

During his interview with a detective with the Waco Police Department, Thames admitted he went overboard while disciplining the child.

When addressing the judge in court, Thames confessed to using excessive force when striking the 3-year-old.

“This case represented holding a Soldier accountable for his domestic violence assault that went far beyond any acceptable level of parental discipline. The prosecution was significant to protect a young child and hold a Soldier accountable for causing harm to someone in the most vulnerable population,” said Capt. Kristyn Dial, prosecutor, Fifth Circuit, Army Office of Special Trial Counsel.

“The conviction was possible based on the close cooperation between the Waco Police Department, the McLennan County District Attorney, and the Army throughout the entire investigation and prosecution process.”

Thames is currently confined at the Bell County Jail in Belton, Texas, awaiting orders to transfer to a military confinement facility.

This case was investigated by the Waco Police Department, the McLennan County District Attorney and the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division’s Central Texas Field Office. It was prosecuted by Dial and Capt. DeJamin M. Bryson, Office of the Staff Judge Advocate, 1st Cavalry Division.

About the Army Office of Special Trial Counsel: The Army Office of Special Trial Counsel is composed of specially trained military lawyers, legal professionals and support staff responsible for the expert prosecution of murder, sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse, kidnapping and other serious criminal offenses. Headquartered at Fort Belvoir, Va., OSTC has eight regional headquarters that oversee 28 field offices located worldwide, including locations in Europe and Korea. For more information visit http://www.army.mil/ostc.

To Report a Crime: If you would like to report a crime, have information about a crime, or have been the subject or survivor of a crime, you can submit anonymous tips to Army CID at http://www.p3tips.com/armycid.
items.titleZh: 被摄像头拍到虐待儿童的陆军中士在胡德堡审判中认罪
items.summaryZh: 一名被Ring摄像头拍到殴打幼童的陆军中士，于10月7日在劳伦斯·威廉姆斯司法中心举行的军事法庭审判中，对家庭暴力指控表示认罪。隶属于第1骑兵师第2装甲旅战斗队第9骑兵团、担任自动化后勤专业兵的保罗·A·泰晤士中士，被军事法官判处一年监禁，并被陆军处以不良品行退伍。法官因其审前已服刑期，给予181天羁押折抵。
zhParas: 得克萨斯州胡德堡——一名被Ring摄像头拍到殴打幼童的陆军中士，在10月7日于劳伦斯·威廉姆斯司法中心举行的军事法庭审判中，对家庭暴力指控表示认罪。
中士保罗·A·泰晤士是第1骑兵师第2装甲旅级战斗队第9骑兵团的一名自动化后勤专员，被军事法官判处一年监禁，并被陆军以品行不良退役。法官就其审前已羁押的时间给予他181天监禁折抵。
2026年1月16日晚，泰晤士在得克萨斯州韦科市女友的公寓里照看其3岁的儿子时，被邻居的Ring门铃摄像头拍到多次拳打该男孩，随后抓住男孩的头颈将他提起。
邻居立即通知韦科警察局，警员随即赶到现场，将泰晤士拘留。
在接受韦科警察局一名警探讯问时，泰晤士承认自己在管教孩子时做得过火。
在法庭上向法官陈述时，泰晤士承认在打这名3岁儿童时使用了过度武力。
本案意味着让一名军人因其家庭暴力袭击行为承担责任，该行为远远超出了任何可接受的父母管教程度。此次起诉意义重大，既是为了保护一名幼童，也是为了让一名军人因伤害最弱势群体中的一员而承担责任，”陆军特别审判律师办公室第五巡回区检察官克里斯汀·戴尔上尉说。
有罪判决之所以能够实现，是因为韦科警察局、麦克伦南县地方检察官办公室和陆军在整个调查和起诉过程中密切合作。
泰晤士目前被关押在得克萨斯州贝尔顿的贝尔县监狱，等待转往军事拘押设施的命令。
本案由韦科警察局、麦克伦南县地方检察官办公室和陆军部刑事调查局中得克萨斯外地办事处调查。由第1骑兵师军法参谋办公室的戴尔和德贾明·M·布赖森上尉提起公诉。
关于陆军特别审判律师办公室：陆军特别审判律师办公室由受过专门训练的军事律师、法律专业人员和辅助人员组成，负责对谋杀、性侵犯、家庭暴力、虐待儿童、绑架和其他严重刑事犯罪进行专业起诉。OSTC总部位于弗吉尼亚州贝尔沃堡，下设八个地区总部，负责监管遍布全球的28个外地办事处，包括欧洲和韩国的办事处。欲了解更多信息，请访问 http://www.army.mil/ostc。
举报犯罪：如果您想举报犯罪、掌握犯罪信息，或是犯罪行为的受害人或幸存者，可以通过 http://www.p3tips.com/armycid 向陆军刑事调查局提交匿名线索。

items.title: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply
items.author: Zita Fletcher
items.summary: The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
items.body:
The Pentagon inked a five-year contract with Raytheon for the steady production of ballistic missile interceptors that use force to destroy targets, rather than explosives.

The $6.3 billion contract, which provides two additional option years, will see Raytheon provide the Defense Department with a continuous supply of Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors manufactured primarily in Tucson, Arizona and Huntsville, Alabama.

“SM-3 Block IB has proven its relevance in combat and this contract helps ensure we can replenish inventories and keep pace with the evolving threats the U.S. Navy, MDA and their partners face around the world,” Raytheon President Phil Jasper said in a statement.

The SM-3 Block IB interceptor belongs to a larger family of “hit-to-kill” SM-3 missile interceptors, which seek and destroy incoming ballistic missiles using sheer speed and momentum.

The Block IB type can be used by land forces and ships and is frequently deployed on vessels due to its range and highly flexible steering. The interceptor tracks flying targets with a two-color infrared seeker and propels itself towards them in short bursts, giving it accuracy at high speed as it homes in on targets.

It is designed to knock short- and intermediate-range ballistic missiles out of the sky when they are halfway to hitting their targets, and has long striking reach. It was used in combat for the first time in 2024 when the U.S. Navy destroyers USS Arleigh Burke and USS Carney fired them to intercept Iranian missiles aimed at targets in Israel.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies named the SM-3 Block IB among “seven critical munitions” in an April report detailing ammunition shortages, alongside Patriot missiles, Precision Strike Missiles, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missiles, Tomahawk Land Attack Missiles and others.

The contract for more SM-3 Block IBs, announced by Raytheon on Thursday, was among five framework agreements the defense giant signed with the Pentagon this February.

The deal comes at a time when the DoD is seeking to avert diminishing munitions stockpiles. National security specialists, defense analysts and foreign policy pundits cautioned in March that the U.S. military’s increased use of missile interceptors during the war with Iran poses strategic risks to integral defense capabilities if fighting spills into a long-term conflict.

Raytheon stated in its release that the contract for SM-3 Block IB supply “supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat and remains central to protecting U.S. forces, allies and critical infrastructure.”

Zita Ballinger Fletcher previously served as editor of Military History Quarterly and Vietnam magazines and as the historian of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. She holds an M.A. with distinction in military history.
items.titleZh: 五角大楼与雷神公司签署63亿美元协议，以补充美国导弹拦截弹供应
items.summaryZh: 雷神公司表示，该合同“支持紧急补充已在战斗中成功使用的导弹防御库存”。
zhParas: 五角大楼与雷神公司签署了一份为期五年的合同，以稳定生产采用动能而非爆炸物摧毁目标的弹道导弹拦截弹。
这份价值63亿美元的合同还包含两个额外的选择权年限；根据合同，雷神公司将向国防部持续供应标准导弹-3 Block IB拦截弹，这些拦截弹主要在亚利桑那州图森和阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔制造。
雷神公司总裁菲尔·贾斯珀在一份声明中表示：“SM-3 Block IB已在实战中证明其价值，这份合同有助于确保我们能够补充库存，并跟上美国海军、导弹防御局及其全球合作伙伴所面临的不断演变的威胁。
SM-3 Block IB拦截弹属于更大的“碰撞杀伤”SM-3导弹拦截弹家族，这类拦截弹依靠纯粹的速度和动量搜寻并摧毁来袭弹道导弹。
Block IB型可由地面部队和舰艇使用，并因其射程和高度灵活的转向能力而经常部署在舰艇上。该拦截弹使用双色红外导引头跟踪飞行目标，并以短促脉冲方式推进飞向目标，从而在高速寻的时保持精度。
它旨在在短程和中程弹道导弹飞向目标的中途将其击落，并具有很远的打击距离。2024年，美国海军驱逐舰“阿利·伯克”号和“卡尼”号发射该拦截弹，拦截瞄准以色列境内目标的伊朗导弹，这是它首次用于实战。
战略与国际研究中心在4月一份详述弹药短缺的报告中，将SM-3 Block IB列为“七种关键弹药”之一，与爱国者导弹、精确打击导弹、末段高空区域防御（THAAD）导弹、战斧对地攻击导弹等并列。
雷神公司周四宣布的增购SM-3 Block IB的合同，是这家防务巨头今年2月与五角大楼签署的五项框架协议之一。
该交易达成之际，美国国防部正寻求避免弹药库存不断减少。国家安全专家、防务分析师和外交政策评论人士在3月警告称，如果战事演变为长期冲突，美军在与伊朗的战争中增加使用导弹拦截弹，将对核心防御能力构成战略风险。
雷神公司在新闻稿中表示，SM-3 Block IB供应合同“支持紧急补充导弹防御库存，该库存已在作战中成功使用，并且仍是保护美军部队、盟友和关键基础设施的核心。
齐塔·巴林杰·弗莱彻曾任《军事历史季刊》和《越南》杂志编辑，以及美国缉毒局历史学家。她以优异成绩获得军事历史学硕士学位。

五角大楼与雷神公司签署了一份为期五年的合同，以稳定生产采用动能而非爆炸物摧毁目标的弹道导弹拦截弹。

这份价值63亿美元的合同还包含两个额外的选择权年限；根据合同，雷神公司将向国防部持续供应标准导弹-3 Block IB拦截弹，这些拦截弹主要在亚利桑那州图森和阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔制造。

雷神公司总裁菲尔·贾斯珀在一份声明中表示：“SM-3 Block IB已在实战中证明其价值，这份合同有助于确保我们能够补充库存，并跟上美国海军、导弹防御局及其全球合作伙伴所面临的不断演变的威胁。

SM-3 Block IB拦截弹属于更大的“碰撞杀伤”SM-3导弹拦截弹家族，这类拦截弹依靠纯粹的速度和动量搜寻并摧毁来袭弹道导弹。

Block IB型可由地面部队和舰艇使用，并因其射程和高度灵活的转向能力而经常部署在舰艇上。该拦截弹使用双色红外导引头跟踪飞行目标，并以短促脉冲方式推进飞向目标，从而在高速寻的时保持精度。

它旨在在短程和中程弹道导弹飞向目标的中途将其击落，并具有很远的打击距离。2024年，美国海军驱逐舰“阿利·伯克”号和“卡尼”号发射该拦截弹，拦截瞄准以色列境内目标的伊朗导弹，这是它首次用于实战。

战略与国际研究中心在4月一份详述弹药短缺的报告中，将SM-3 Block IB列为“七种关键弹药”之一，与爱国者导弹、精确打击导弹、末段高空区域防御（THAAD）导弹、战斧对地攻击导弹等并列。

雷神公司周四宣布的增购SM-3 Block IB的合同，是这家防务巨头今年2月与五角大楼签署的五项框架协议之一。

该交易达成之际，美国国防部正寻求避免弹药库存不断减少。国家安全专家、防务分析师和外交政策评论人士在3月警告称，如果战事演变为长期冲突，美军在与伊朗的战争中增加使用导弹拦截弹，将对核心防御能力构成战略风险。

雷神公司在新闻稿中表示，SM-3 Block IB供应合同“支持紧急补充导弹防御库存，该库存已在作战中成功使用，并且仍是保护美军部队、盟友和关键基础设施的核心。

齐塔·巴林杰·弗莱彻曾任《军事历史季刊》和《越南》杂志编辑，以及美国缉毒局历史学家。她以优异成绩获得军事历史学硕士学位。

items.title: Fort Hood Soldier who attempted to kill colleague sentenced to more than 17 years in prison
items.author: Michelle McCaskill
items.summary: An Army private who purposely crashed his car in an attempt to kill a fellow Soldier pleaded guilty to attempted unpremeditated murder during his court-martial Oct. 1 at the Lawrence Williams Judicial Center. Clarkston, 20, an Army cook assigned to the 1st Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, was sentenced by the military judge to 17 years and eight months in prison and a dishonorable discharge from the Army. items.body:
FORT HOOD, Texas – An Army private who purposely crashed his car in an attempt to kill a fellow Soldier pleaded guilty to attempted unpremeditated murder during his court-martial Oct. 1 at the Lawrence Williams Judicial Center.

Pvt. James D. Clarkston, 20, an Army cook assigned to the 1st Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, was sentenced by the military judge to 17 years and eight months in prison and a dishonorable discharge from the Army.

In addition to the attempted unpremeditated murder charge, Clarkston also pleaded guilty to wrongful use of marijuana, failure to obey a general order, and damaging non-military property.

Clarkston was reported by the victim, a fellow cook in his unit, to command leadership for being high at work.

As a result, leadership removed Clarkston from duty and conducted a Probable Cause Urinalysis which revealed he had been using prohibited substances.

Shortly afterwards on Dec. 15, 2025, Clarkston was in his vehicle with the victim when he confronted him about the report to leadership. Upset that he’d been reported, Clarkston began driving recklessly through Fort Hood at a high rate of speed, running through stop signs and crosswalks, ultimately crashing his car into a utility pole with the intent to kill himself and the victim. The crash caused the vehicle to roll over multiple times, hitting several cars in a nearby parking lot.

Fort Hood Military Police and emergency services responded to the incident, transporting the victim and Clarkston to the Carl R. Darnell Army Medical Center where they were treated for minor injuries.

The Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division initiated an investigation and interviewed multiple witnesses, as well as the military police who responded to the crash. They told agents that Clarkston confessed immediately after the incident to purposely crashing the vehicle. This was confirmed by Army CID agents when reconstructing the crash scene.

“Pvt. Clarkston took intentional acts aimed at ending the life of another Soldier. The fact that the victim survived is a miracle, but it does not excuse Pvt. Clarkston’s actions and intent,” said Capt. Mark L. Wegzyn, prosecutor, Fifth Circuit, Army Office of Special Trial Counsel.

“This sentence sends a clear and unmistakable message that unlawful violence cannot, and will not, be tolerated in the United States Army. We are incredibly grateful for the bravery of the victim in this case for coming forward and seeing the process through to the end.”

“This case demonstrates why a thorough investigation is essential,” said Special Agent in Charge Lane Allen, Army CID’s Central Texas Field Office.

“What may initially appear to be a traffic accident or isolated incident can reveal deliberate criminal conduct when examined closely. Violence against a fellow Soldier is unacceptable, and Army CID remains committed to following the facts and providing the evidence necessary to seek accountability.”

Clarkston will serve his prison sentence at the United States Disciplinary Barracks at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

This case was investigated by Army CID’s Central Texas Field Office and the Fort Hood Military Police. It was prosecuted by Wegzyn and Capt. Calvin Maynard, Office of the Staff Judge Advocate, 1st Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division.

About the Army Office of Special Trial Counsel: The Army Office of Special Trial Counsel is composed of specially trained military lawyers, legal professionals and support staff responsible for the expert prosecution of murder, sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse, kidnapping and other serious criminal offenses. Headquartered at Fort Belvoir, Va., OSTC has eight regional headquarters that oversee 28 field offices located worldwide, including locations in Europe and Korea. For more information visit www.army.mil/ostc.

To Report a Crime: If you would like to report a crime, have information about a crime, or have been the subject or survivor of a crime, you can submit anonymous tips to Army CID at www.p3tips.com/armycid.
items.titleZh: 企图杀害战友的胡德堡陆军士兵被判处逾17年监禁
items.summaryZh: 一名故意驾车撞车以企图杀害一名战友的陆军列兵，于10月1日在劳伦斯·威廉姆斯司法中心接受军事法庭审判时，对非预谋谋杀未遂指控认罪。20岁的陆军列兵詹姆斯·D·克拉克森是第1骑兵师第1装甲旅级战斗队的一名陆军炊事兵，被军事法官判处17年8个月监禁，并被陆军开除军籍（不名誉退役）。除非预谋谋杀未遂指控外，
zhParas: 德克萨斯州胡德堡——一名故意驾车撞车以企图杀害一名战友的陆军列兵，于10月1日在劳伦斯·威廉姆斯司法中心接受军事法庭审判时，对非预谋谋杀未遂指控认罪。
20岁的陆军列兵詹姆斯·D·克拉克森是第1骑兵师第1装甲旅级战斗队的一名陆军炊事兵，被军事法官判处17年零8个月监禁，并被陆军不名誉退役。
除非预谋谋杀未遂指控外，克拉克森还对不当使用大麻、未遵守一般命令以及损坏非军事财产认罪。
克拉克森被其所在部队的另一名炊事兵——即受害人——向部队领导层举报，原因是他在工作时处于吸毒后的亢奋状态。
因此，领导层解除了克拉克森的职务，并进行了有合理根据的尿检，结果显示他一直使用违禁物质。
不久之后，即2025年12月15日，克拉克森与受害人同处其车内，并就向领导层举报一事与受害人当面对质。因被举报而恼怒，克拉克森开始以高速在胡德堡内鲁莽驾驶，冲过停车标志和人行横道，最终故意将车撞向一根电线杆，意图杀死自己和受害人。撞击导致车辆多次翻滚，并撞上附近停车场内的数辆汽车。
胡德堡宪兵和应急部门对事件作出响应，将受害者和克拉克森送往卡尔·R·达内尔陆军医疗中心，在那里两人因轻伤接受治疗。
美国陆军部刑事调查局启动调查，并询问了多名证人以及响应这起撞车事件的宪兵。他们告诉探员，克拉克森在事件发生后立即承认故意撞车。陆军刑事调查局探员在重建事故现场时证实了这一点。
列兵克拉克森采取了旨在终结另一名士兵生命的故意行为。受害者幸存下来是奇迹，但这不能开脱列兵克拉克森的行为和意图，”陆军特别审判顾问办公室第五巡回区检察官马克·L·韦格津上尉说。
这一判决发出明确无误的信息：非法暴力在美国陆军中不能、也绝不会被容忍。我们无比感激本案受害者的勇敢，他挺身而出并坚持走完整个程序。
本案表明为什么彻底调查至关重要，”陆军刑事调查局得克萨斯州中部外地办事处主管特别探员莱恩·艾伦说。
最初看似交通事故或孤立事件的情况，在仔细审查后可能揭示出蓄意犯罪行为。对战友的暴力不可接受，陆军刑事调查局仍致力于追查事实，并提供寻求问责所需的证据。
克拉克斯顿将在堪萨斯州莱文沃思堡的美国纪律兵营服刑。
本案由陆军刑事调查局中得克萨斯外地办事处和胡德堡宪兵调查，并由第1骑兵师第1装甲旅级战斗队军法参谋办公室的韦格津和卡尔文·梅纳德上尉提起公诉。
关于陆军特别审判律师办公室：陆军特别审判律师办公室由经过专门训练的军事律师、法律专业人员和辅助人员组成，负责对谋杀、性侵犯、家庭暴力、虐待儿童、绑架及其他严重刑事犯罪进行专业起诉。该办公室总部位于弗吉尼亚州贝尔沃堡，下设八个地区总部，负责监督分布在全球的28个外地办事处，包括在欧洲和韩国的办公地点。欲了解更多信息，请访问 www.army.mil/ostc。
举报犯罪：如果您想举报犯罪、掌握与犯罪有关的信息，或是犯罪的受害对象或幸存者，可通过 www.p3tips.com/armycid 向陆军刑事调查局提交匿名线索。

items.title: BAE Lands Contract for F-35 Block 4 Electronic Warfare Systems
items.author: Steve Losey
items.summary: BAE Systems has received a contract from Lockheed Martin to install an upgraded Block 4 electronic warfare system into new F-35 Joint Strike Fighters, as well as to retrofit some older jets. The post BAE Lands Contract for F-35 Block 4 Electronic Warfare Systems appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
BAE Systems has received a contract from Lockheed Martin to install an upgraded Block 4 electronic warfare system into new F-35 Joint Strike Fighters, as well as to retrofit some older jets.

BAE’s AN/ASQ-239 EW systems will be installed on lots 20 to 22 of the F-35, the company said in an Oct. 6 statement, and some older F-35s with previous versions of the EW system will be retrofitted to have the latest version installed.

“BAE Systems has been the EW supplier for the F-35 program for the past 21 years, successfully designing and developing the Block 1, Block 2, and Block 3 configurations” of the AN/ASQ-239, Amber Dolan, BAE’s vice president of F-35 solutions, said in a follow-up statement to Air & Space Forces Magazine. “We are currently developing Block 4 systems that can accelerate the delivery of advanced EW capabilities via adaptable hardware and incremental software updates.”

The updated EW suite is part of a broader program of upgrades to the Lockheed Martin-made F-35, collectively referred to as Block 4. Lockheed previously awarded BAE a $491 million contract for the F-35 EW systems in 2023, and another $493 million contract in 2021.

The Block 4 EW systems that will be in F-35 lots 20 and beyond “offer improvements in threat detection, situational awareness, and capabilities to counter modern threats,” Dolan said.

BAE declined to say how much the contract is worth and how many EW systems it will deliver for new jets and retrofits. The company said it has delivered more than 1,500 EW systems for the F-35 so far.

BAE said the AN/ASQ-239 system provides both offensive and defensive EW capabilities, which give pilots a 360-degree view of the battlefield and allow the F-35 to operate in environments protected by enemy fighters, missiles, drones, or integrated air defense systems. Its passive long-range sensing capabilities combine with high-speed signal processing and advanced algorithms to allow pilots to detect and counter threats before an enemy can act, the company said. The system’s software can also be quickly updated to account for new threats.

A previous upgrade to the AN/ASQ-239 EW system—called the Digital Channelized Receiver/Techniques Generator and Tuner Insertion Program, or DTIP—was launched in 2018. Those DTIP improvements allowed for previous versions of the EW system to be condensed into a smaller footprint that required less power, which created space for the new Block 4 modernization.

BAE said it has made investments in facilities—including the 2022 opening of a new 200,000-square-foot engineering and production facility in Manchester, N.H.—to help design and develop new EW systems. BAE also designs and manufactures EW systems at facilities in Merrimack, N.H., Nashua, N.H., and Austin, Texas.
items.titleZh: BAE获得F-35 Block 4电子战系统合同
items.summaryZh: BAE系统公司已从洛克希德·马丁公司获得一份合同，将升级版Block 4电子战系统安装到新的F-35联合攻击战斗机上，并对部分较旧战机进行改装。文章《BAE获得F-35 Block 4电子战系统合同》最初发表于《Air & Space Forces Magazine》。
zhParas: BAE系统公司已从洛克希德·马丁公司获得一份合同，将升级版Block 4电子战系统安装到新的F-35联合攻击战斗机上，并对部分较旧战机进行改装。
BAE系统公司10月6日在一份声明中表示，其AN/ASQ-239电子战系统将安装到F-35的第20至第22批次上，部分搭载此前版本电子战系统的较旧F-35也将被改装，以安装最新版本。
过去21年来，BAE系统公司一直是F-35项目的电子战供应商，成功设计并开发了AN/ASQ-239的Block 1、Block 2和Block 3配置，”BAE系统公司F-35解决方案副总裁安伯·多兰在给《空天力量》杂志的后续声明中说。“我们目前正在开发Block 4系统，可通过适应性硬件和增量软件更新，加速交付先进电子战能力。
更新后的电子战套件是洛克希德·马丁制造的F-35更广泛升级计划的一部分，统称为Block 4。洛克希德公司此前于2023年授予BAE系统公司一份价值4.91亿美元的F-35电子战系统合同，并于2021年授予另一份价值4.93亿美元的合同。
多兰表示，将装备F-35第20批次及以后批次的Block 4电子战系统“在威胁探测、态势感知以及对抗现代威胁的能力方面有所提升”。
BAE系统公司拒绝透露该合同价值多少，以及将为新战机交付多少套电子战系统、为改装交付多少套。该公司表示，迄今为止已为F-35交付超过1500套电子战系统。
BAE表示，AN/ASQ-239系统同时提供进攻性和防御性电子战能力，使飞行员拥有360度战场视野，并让F-35能够在敌方战斗机、导弹、无人机或一体化防空系统保护的环境中作战。该公司称，其被动远程感知能力与高速信号处理和先进算法相结合，使飞行员能够在敌方采取行动之前探测并反制威胁。该系统的软件还可以快速更新，以应对新的威胁。
AN/ASQ-239电子战系统此前的一项升级——称为数字信道化接收机/技术发生器与调谐器插入项目（DTIP）——于2018年启动。这些DTIP改进使此前版本的电子战系统得以压缩为占用空间更小、所需功率更低的形态，从而为新的Block 4现代化升级腾出空间。

items.title: Readout of U.S. Naval Forces Central Command/U.S. 5th Fleet/Combined Maritime Forces Vice Adm. Curt Renshaw’s Meeting with Royal Saudi Defense Leaders
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: TAMPA, Fla. -- Commander of U.S. Naval Forces Central Command/U.S. 5th Fleet/Combined Maritime Forces (NAVCENT/C5F/CMF) Vice Adm. Curt Renshaw met with Saudi defense leaders during a trip to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct. 6-7.
items.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- U.S. Naval Forces Central Command/U.S. 5th Fleet/Combined Maritime Forces Commander Vice Adm. Curt Renshaw met with Saudi defense leaders during a trip to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct. 6-7.

The meetings included discussions with H.E. General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili, the chief of general staff; Vice Adm. Mohammed Al-Ghuraybi, commander, Royal Saudi Naval Forces; Vice Adm. Fahad Al Ghofaily, the deputy chief of defense; Lt. Gen. Fahad al-Salman, commander, Saudi Joint Forces Command; and Rear Adm. Abdullah al-Mutairi, naval component commander, Saudi Joint Forces Command. Renshaw also met with Chargé d’Affaires and additional country team personnel.

The discussions focused on the enduring partnership between the two militaries and enhancing interoperability between the navies of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the U.S.

The leaders explored opportunities to promote freedom of navigation in the region and exchanged views on regional security challenges.

Renshaw acknowledged the significant contributions by Saudi Arabia to regional security, specifically highlighting the role Saudi Arabian Armed Forces take in promoting stability and prosperity alongside global and regional partners.

items.summaryZh: 佛罗里达州坦帕——美国海军中央司令部/美国第五舰队/联合海上力量司令、海军中将库特·伦肖于10月6日至7日访问沙特阿拉伯利雅得期间，会见了沙特国防领导人。

会晤对象包括沙特总参谋长法亚德·本·哈米德·鲁瓦伊利上将阁下、沙特皇家海军司令穆罕默德·古莱比海军中将、国防副参谋长法赫德·戈法伊利海军中将、沙特联合部队司令部司令法赫德·萨勒曼中将，以及沙特联合部队司令部海军组成部队司令阿卜杜拉·穆塔伊里少将。伦肖还会见了临时代办及其他国家团队人员。
讨论重点围绕两军之间持久的伙伴关系，以及加强沙特阿拉伯王国海军与美国海军之间的互操作性。
双方领导人探讨了促进地区航行自由的机会，并就地区安全挑战交换了意见。

items.title: Why I Serve: Airman Follows Family Legacy of Service and Caring for Others
items.author: Bernhard Lashleyleidner
items.summary: In the Emergency Department at Landstuhl Regional Medical Center, medical personnel must remain focused as they respond to patients who need urgent care. Among them is U.S. Air Force Senior Airman Ian Guarisco, a medic whose work is guided by a family tradition of military service and a lifelong interest in medicine. Guarisco’s decision to serve was influenced by the example set by both of his grandfathers Guarisco’s decision to serve was influenced by the example set by both of his grandfathers
items.body:
LANDSTUHL, Germany — In the Emergency Department at Landstuhl Regional Medical Center, medical personnel must remain focused as they respond to patients who need urgent care. Among them is U.S. Air Force Senior Airman Ian Guarisco, a medic whose work is guided by a family tradition of military service and a lifelong interest in medicine.

Guarisco’s decision to serve was influenced by the example set by both of his grandfathers who served in the military, as well as a cousin currently serving in the Marine Corps.

“Both of my grandfathers served, and my cousin is currently in the Marine Corps. I have always looked up to the people who wear the uniform,” Guarisco said. “I wanted to follow in their footsteps, be part of something bigger than myself, and make a real difference ."

While his grandfathers gave him a blueprint for military service, his interest in medicine began at home. His mother spent 20 years as an intensive care nurse, and his father works as an emergency medicine nurse practitioner. Growing up around health care professionals gave Guarisco an early appreciation for the work involved in caring for others.

“Seeing the difference, they made every day sparked my own curiosity,” Guarisco said. “I knew early on that medicine was the only path for me.”

The example set by his family also shaped his understanding of service, sacrifice, and the importance of supporting others.

Today, Guarisco applies those lessons in the LRMC Emergency Department. The medical center treats service members and other eligible patients from across Europe, Africa, and the Middle East, presenting medical personnel with a wide range of cases and challenges.

For Guarisco, the work means helping patients through some of the most difficult moments.

“ There is something incredibly meaningful about being there for people when they are sick and vulnerable,” Guarisco said. “Just being able to help them feel a little better is the most rewarding part of my job.”

He said his family is incredibly proud that I’ve found a way to combine our family's two greatest passions: serving the country and caring for others .

His dedication to patient care has also earned recognition from his colleagues.

Sgt. Jonathan Baczynski, a noncommissioned officer in LRMC’s Emergency Department, said Guarisco consistently demonstrates professionalism and technical skills.

"He is always on top of everything that needs to be done,” Baczynski said. "Anytime he works with an ill patient, he does it exceptionally well,” Baczynski said. “He is simply an outstanding technician and service member."

For Guarisco, military service and medicine are closely connected. The values he learned from his family continue to guide him as he cares for patients and supports the LRMC mission, carrying forward a legacy of service that began generations before him.

items.titleZh: 我为何服役：空军上等兵传承家族服役与关爱他人的传统
zhParas: 德国兰德斯图尔——在兰德斯图尔地区医疗中心急诊科，医务人员在救治需要紧急护理的患者时必须保持专注。他们当中就有美国空军上等兵伊恩·瓜里斯科，他是一名医疗兵，其工作受家族从军传统和对医学的终身兴趣指引。
瓜里斯科决定服役，受到他两位曾在军队服役的祖父以及一位目前正在海军陆战队服役的表亲的榜样影响。
我的两位祖父都曾服役，我的表亲目前也在海军陆战队。我一直敬仰穿军装的人，”瓜里斯科说。“我想追随他们的脚步，成为比自己更宏大事业的一部分，并真正带来改变。
祖父们为他提供了从军的蓝图，而他对医学的兴趣则始于家庭。他的母亲当了20年重症监护护士，父亲则是一名急诊医学高级执业护士。在医护人员身边长大，使瓜里斯科很早就体会到照顾他人所涉及的工作。
看到他们每天带来的改变，激发了我自己的好奇心，”瓜里斯科说。“我很早就知道，医学是我唯一的道路。
家人树立的榜样也塑造了他对服役、牺牲以及支持他人的重要性的理解。
如今，瓜里斯科在LRMC急诊科运用这些经验。该医疗中心收治来自欧洲、非洲和中东各地的军人及其他符合资格的患者，这使医务人员面对各种各样的病例和挑战。
对瓜里斯科而言，这项工作意味着帮助患者度过一些最艰难的时刻。
当人们生病、脆弱时，能陪伴在他们身边，这件事有着极其深刻的意义，”瓜里斯科说。“只要能帮他们感觉稍微好一点，就是我工作中最有成就感的部分。
他说，他的家人为我能找到一种把我们家庭最热爱的两件事结合起来的方式而感到无比自豪：报效国家和关爱他人。
他对患者护理的奉献也赢得了同事们的认可。
LRMC急诊科的一名士官乔纳森·巴琴斯基中士表示，瓜里斯科始终展现出专业素养和技术能力。
他总是掌控着一切需要完成的事，”巴琴斯基说。“每当他照料患病患者时，都做得极其出色，”巴琴斯基说。“他简直就是一名杰出的医疗技师和军人。
对瓜里斯科来说，军旅服役与医学密不可分。他从家人身上学到的价值观，继续指引他照护患者并支持LRMC的使命，延续着始于他之前数代人的服役传承。

items.title: NCNG State Partnership Program Director receives the National Army Medal from the Republic of Moldova
items.author: SGT Brittany Burton
items.summary: RALEIGH, N.C. — U.S. Army Lt. Col. Michal Sterling, North Carolina National Guard State Partnership Program director assigned to the 60th Troop Command, was awarded the National Army Medal by Brig. Gen. Sergiu Cirimpei, Defense Attaché, on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, Republic of Moldova at Joint Force Headquarters in Raleigh, N.C., on Oct. 8, 2026. This award was given to recognize his commitment, leadership, and contributions to the enduring partnership between the two nations.
items.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. — U.S. Army Lt. Col. Michal Sterling, North Carolina National Guard State Partnership Program director assigned to the 60th Troop Command, was awarded the National Army Medal by Brig. Gen. Sergiu Cirimpei, Defense, Military, and Air Attaché to the U.S., on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, Republic of Moldova at Joint Force Headquarters in Raleigh, N.C., on Oct. 8, 2026. The award recognized his commitment, leadership, and contributions to the enduring partnership between the two nations.

“I’m happy to present this award to you for all your hard work and leadership shown to Moldova," said Brig. Gen. Sergiu Cirimpei,

Sterling's recognition reflects years of work strengthening the relationship between North Carolina and Moldova through the National Guard’s State Partnership Program, a partnership established in 1996. In 2017, then Capt. Sterling began serving as the Bilateral Affairs officer for Moldova, working to strengthen military cooperation and maintain relationships between the NCNG and its Moldovan counterparts.

Two years later, in 2019, then-Maj. Sterling became the NCNG’s State Partnership Program director, taking on responsibility for coordinating engagements and advocating the state’s international partnership. The success of this partnership was recognized in 2023, when the NCNG and Moldova received the National Guard Bureau’s State Partnership of the Year award, highlighting the hard work and dedication between the two partners and their continued commitment to shared security objectives.

As the SPP director, Sterling oversaw partnerships with Moldova, Botswana, Malawi, and Zambia, coordinating military-to-military and civilian engagements designed to strengthen partner capabilities and promote long-term self-reliance. Under his leadership, the program directed 57 security cooperation events across Europe and Africa, giving NCNG personnel and international partners opportunities to exchange knowledge, develop capabilities, and build relationships that extend beyond individual missions.

In addition to receiving Moldova’s National Army Medal, the National Guard Bureau recognized Sterling as the 2025 State Partnership Program Director of the Year for his management of the NCNG's partnerships. As SPP director, one of Sterling's duties was to oversee the program's annual funding allocations supporting the two partners' security cooperation objectives, ensuring resources aligned with strategic priorities and partnership goals.

“You’ve been such a great asset and leader to both NCNG and the great State of North Carolina," said Secretary Elaine Marshall, North Carolina's Secretary of State. "Congratulations and thank you for all that you do."

Sterling’s recognition highlights the impact of a continued commitment, demonstrating how sustained relationships and strategic leadership can strengthen both NCNG and its international partners. (U.S. Army story by Sgt. Brittany Burton)
items.titleZh: 北卡罗来纳国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划主任获摩尔多瓦共和国授予国家陆军奖章
items.summaryZh: 罗利，北卡罗来纳州——美国陆军中校米哈尔·斯特林（Michal Sterling），北卡罗来纳国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划主任，隶属第60部队司令部，于2026年10月8日在北卡罗来纳州罗利联合部队司令部，由摩尔多瓦共和国国防部代表、驻美国国防、军事和空军武官谢尔久·奇林佩伊准将（Brig. Gen. Sergiu Cirimpei）授予国家陆军奖章。该奖项表彰他对两国持久伙伴关系的承诺、领导力和贡献。
zhParas: 罗利，北卡罗来纳州——美国陆军中校米哈尔·斯特林（Michal Sterling），北卡罗来纳国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划主任，隶属第60部队司令部，于2026年10月8日在北卡罗来纳州罗利联合部队司令部，由摩尔多瓦共和国国防部代表、驻美国国防、军事和空军武官谢尔久·奇林佩伊准将（Brig. Gen. Sergiu Cirimpei）授予国家陆军奖章。该奖项表彰他对两国持久伙伴关系的承诺、领导力和贡献。
我很高兴将这一奖项颁发给你，以表彰你为摩尔多瓦展现出的所有辛勤工作和领导力，”谢尔久·奇林佩伊准将说道，
斯特林获得的表彰反映了多年来通过国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划加强北卡罗来纳州与摩尔多瓦关系的工作，该伙伴关系成立于1996年。2017年，时任上尉的斯特林开始担任摩尔多瓦双边事务官，致力于加强军事合作并维护北卡罗来纳国民警卫队与其摩尔多瓦同行之间的关系。
两年后，2019年，时任少校的斯特林成为北卡罗来纳国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划主任，负责协调交流活动并倡导该州的国际伙伴关系。这一伙伴关系的成功在2023年得到认可，北卡罗来纳国民警卫队和摩尔多瓦获得了国民警卫队局颁发的年度州伙伴关系奖，彰显了两个伙伴之间的辛勤工作和奉献精神，以及他们对共同安全目标的持续承诺。
作为州伙伴关系计划主任，斯特林负责监督与摩尔多瓦、博茨瓦纳、马拉维和赞比亚的伙伴关系，协调旨在加强伙伴能力并促进长期自力更生的军事对军事和民事交流活动。在他的领导下，该计划指导了欧洲和非洲的57项安全合作活动，为北卡罗来纳国民警卫队人员和国际伙伴提供了交流知识、发展能力并建立超越单个任务的关系的机会。
除了获得摩尔多瓦的国家陆军奖章外，国民警卫队局还表彰斯特林为2025年度州伙伴关系计划主任，以肯定他对北卡罗来纳国民警卫队伙伴关系的管理。作为州伙伴关系计划主任，斯特林的职责之一是监督该计划支持两个伙伴安全合作目标的年度资金分配，确保资源与战略优先事项和伙伴关系目标保持一致。
对北卡罗来纳国民警卫队（NCNG）和伟大的北卡罗来纳州而言，您一直是极为宝贵的人才和领导者，”北卡罗来纳州州务卿伊莱恩·马歇尔说。“祝贺您，并感谢您所做的一切。
斯特林获得的表彰凸显了持续投入的影响，表明持久关系和战略领导力如何能够加强北卡罗来纳国民警卫队（NCNG）及其国际伙伴。（美国陆军，布列塔尼·伯顿中士撰文）

items.title: MICC closes fiscal 2026 with $6.8 billion in Army contracting support
items.author: Tish Williamson
items.summary: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command closed fiscal year 2026 with more than 21,450 contracting actions valued at approximately $6.8 billion, including $2.9 billion awarded to American small businesses, as the command expanded its role in Army modernization and innovative acquisition. The command also managed more than 299,000 Government Purchase Card transactions valued at more than $520 million, providing additional purchasing power support to Soldiers, installations and mission par
items.body:
JOINT BASE SAN ANTONIO-FORT SAM HOUSTON, Texas — The Mission and Installation Contracting Command closed fiscal year 2026 with more than 21,450 contracting actions valued at approximately $6.8 billion, including $2.9 billion awarded to American small businesses, as the command expanded its role in Army modernization and innovative acquisition.

The command also managed more than 299,000 Government Purchase Card transactions valued at more than $520 million, providing additional purchasing power in support of Soldiers, installations and mission partners across the Army.

The results reflect over a $1 billion increase in contracting obligations over fiscal 2025 , driven largely by growing facility modernization requirements, expanded acquisition authorities, and adding 410th Contracting Support Brigade to MICC’s portfolio in January .

“Some growth was expected as we welcomed the 410th Contracting Support Brigade into the command,” said Command Sgt. Maj. JennyAnne Bright, MICC command sergeant major , in the MICC command team Oct. 1 message to the workforce .

“But $1 billion in growth reflects the growing demand for your expertise and your ability to deliver contracting solutions to Soldiers and our mission partners at the point of need.”

David Markelz, deputy director of MICC Contracting Operations, attributed much of the increase to facility modernization initiatives that have expanded the command’s contracting responsibilities.

“ New legislation and updated https://safe.menlosecurity.com/doc/docview/viewer/docN1987DD0EE1BB421b71bea1981c758cc762275de2744473ce785c6a82335a7fe32a2649805e0e have enabled MICC to directly support construction and modernization requirements historically managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers,” Markelz said. The command responded by employing a broader range of acquisition authorities, including Other Transactions Authorities (OTAs), Small Business Innovation Research Phase (SBIR) III and Multiple Award Task Orders (MATOCs) to address complex, multilayered regional requirements and expand opportunities for collaboration with industry.

“By employing a broader array of acquisition authorities, the MICC is better positioned than ever to meet the evolving needs of the Army and deliver timely, mission‑focused results.”

Among the year’s major accomplishments were the Facilities, Operations, Readiness, Growth and Experience, or FORGE, initiatives, which consolidated multiple modernization requirements into larger, coordinated acquisition efforts that bundled related requirements to deliver effective outcomes instead of isolating projects due to rigid processes.

At Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, MICC awarded a $169.1 million Other Transaction agreement supporting 17 modernization projects . At Anniston Army Depot, Alabama, another MICC FORGE initiative established approximately $987 million in modernization efforts, with about $658 million initially obligated to support critical military construction and improvements to the Army’s Organic Industrial Base.

Other notable MICC efforts included a roughly $201 million OTA for the Fort Polk Rotational Unit Billeting Area (RUBA) , using construction-scale additive manufacturing, and a similar approximately $13 million OTA billeting effort at McGregor Range, New Mexico.

MICC also established its first enterprise-wide architect-engineer contracting capability, awarding 20 indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contracts across five geographic regions to support planning, design and construction-related services.

Additional enterprise solutions included the https://samclerk.com/opportunity/dept-of-defense/W51EW7-26-R-A002, providing seven Army garrisons access to competed regional construction and repair capacity, and two SBIR III contracting vehicles through Field Directorate Office, Fort Eustis, Virginia with a combined $800 million ceiling for training support and human-performance infrastructure.

“You showed that the MICC is prepared to meet demands differently,” said Brig. Gen. Freddy L. Adams, MICC commanding general , in the command’s fiscal year-end message . “You helped us expand our use of innovative acquisition tools, including Other Transaction Authorities, Small Business Innovation Research Phase III pathways and enterprise contracting solutions that help us move faster and deliver capability where it matters most.”

Beyond modernization, MICC continued its longstanding commitment to American small businesses, exceeding its assigned small business goals for the 12th consecutive year despite workforce reductions and increasingly complex requirements.

“Exceeding our small business goals across the board for a 12th consecutive year is a phenomenal achievement by our contracting and small business professionals,” said Luis Trinidad, director of the Army Contracting Command-MICC Office of Small Business Programs. “Operating with a 30% reduction in personnel, our team rose to meet a more demanding workload.”

With the growth year in contracting, Trinidad said the command’s small business-eligible dollars also increased by $104.8 million, requiring more detailed reviews of higher-value and increasingly complex acquisition packages.

“By conducting thorough, detailed reviews on every single opportunity,” Trinidad said, “our team ensured we met all of our targets while delivering vital small business capabilities and services that directly support the Warfighter."

Looking ahead to fiscal year 2027 , MICC anticipates continued growth in modernization requirements, increased demand for enterprise contracting solutions and greater use of innovative acquisition authorities tailored to specific mission and Soldier needs.

MICC Deputy to the Commanding General, Clay Cole also praised the workforce in the closeout message for helping the command achieve priorities align with the command’s 2026-2027 Campaign Plan , emphasizing people and forging contract experts, readiness, mission execution and transformation.

“Together, we established our first enterprise-wide architect-engineer contracting capability, spanning the continental United States and Puerto Rico; accelerated critical sustainment, restoration and modernization requirements; and expanded housing, barracks and other quality-of-life support,” Cole said.

“Those accomplishments demonstrate what happens when contracting professionals are empowered to innovate, collaborate, and stay focused on the warfighter.”

The fiscal year closeout also coincided with the contracting command’s 18th anniversary. Established under the Army Contracting Command as the Installation Contracting Command Oct. 1, 2008, and redesignated as MICC the following day, the organization has evolved into a critical contracting powerhouse for Army readiness and modernization.

As the command enters fiscal year 2027, the command team also emphasized that the long list of accomplishments since its inception reflects the expertise and dedication of contracting professionals across its geographically dispersed workforce.

“In just two short decades, MICC has grown into an indispensable element of the Army’s mission, and that legacy is entirely due to the hard work and excellence of professionals like you,” Adams said.

The leaders thanked the MICC workforce and Soldiers, urging them to take a moment to reflect on all that they accomplished while maintaining the positive momentum as they begin the new fiscal year.

About the MICC Headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio -Fort Sam Houston, Texas, the Mission and Installation Contracting Command consists of about 1,500 military and civilian members who are responsible for contracting goods and services in support of Soldiers as well as readying trained contracting units for the operating force and contingency environment when called upon. A subordinate command of the Army Contracting Command and the Army Materiel Command, MICC contracts are vital in feeding more than 200,000 Soldiers every day, providing many daily base operations support services at installations, facilitate training in the preparation of more than 100,000 conventional force members annually, training more than 500,000 students each year, and maintaining more than 14.4 million acres of land and 170,000 structures. See also the MICC Fact Sheet .
items.titleZh: 任务与设施合同司令部以68亿美元陆军合同支持结束2026财年
items.summaryZh: 任务与设施合同司令部以超过21,450项合同行动、价值约68亿美元结束2026财年，其中包括授予美国小企业的29亿美元，同时该司令部扩大了其在陆军现代化和创新采办中的作用。该司令部还管理了超过299,000笔政府采购卡交易，价值超过5.2亿美元，为士兵、设施和任务伙伴提供额外的购买力支持。
zhParas: 得克萨斯州圣安东尼奥-萨姆休斯敦堡联合基地——任务与设施合同司令部以超过21,450项合同行动、价值约68亿美元结束2026财年，其中包括授予美国小企业的29亿美元，同时该司令部扩大了其在陆军现代化和创新采办中的作用。
该司令部还管理了超过299,000笔政府采购卡交易，价值超过5.2亿美元，为支持整个陆军的士兵、设施和任务伙伴提供了额外的购买力。
这些结果反映出合同义务比2025财年增加超过10亿美元，主要驱动因素是不断增长的设施现代化需求、扩大的采办权限，以及1月将第410合同保障旅纳入MICC的业务组合。
当我们欢迎第410合同保障旅加入该司令部时，一些增长是预料之中的，”MICC指挥军士长珍妮安妮·布赖特在MICC指挥团队10月1日致全体工作人员的信中说。
但10亿美元的增长反映了对你们专业能力日益增长的需求，以及你们在需求点向士兵和我们的任务伙伴提供合同解决方案的能力。
MICC合同运营副主任戴维·马凯尔兹将大部分增长归因于设施现代化举措，这些举措扩大了该司令部的合同职责。

新立法和更新的 https://safe.menlosecurity.com/doc/docview/viewer/docN1987DD0EE1BB421b71bea1981c758cc762275de2744473ce785c6a82335a7fe32a2649805e0e 使 MICC 能够直接支持历史上由美国陆军工程兵团管理的建设和现代化需求，”Markelz 说。该司令部通过采用更广泛的采购授权作为回应，包括其他交易授权（OTA）、小企业创新研究第三阶段（SBIR III）和多项授标任务订单（MATOC），以应对复杂、多层次的区域需求，并扩大与工业界合作的机会。
通过采用更广泛的采购授权，MICC 比以往任何时候都更有能力满足陆军不断变化的需求，并及时交付以任务为重点的成果。
年度主要成就包括设施、运营、战备、增长与经验（FORGE）倡议，这些倡议将多项现代化需求整合为更大规模、协调一致的采购工作，将相关需求打包，以交付有效成果，而不是因僵化流程而将项目割裂开来。
在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地，MICC 授予了一份价值 1.691 亿美元的其他交易协议，支持 17 个现代化项目。在阿拉巴马州安尼斯顿陆军仓库，另一项 MICC FORGE 倡议确立了约 9.87 亿美元的现代化工作，其中约 6.58 亿美元初步承付，用于支持关键军事建设和陆军有机工业基础的改进。
MICC 的其他显著工作包括一项约 2.01 亿美元的其他交易协议，用于波尔克堡轮换部队住宿区（RUBA），采用建筑规模增材制造；以及在新墨西哥州麦格雷戈靶场开展的类似约 1300 万美元 OTA 住宿工作。
MICC 还建立了其首个全企业范围的建筑-工程合同能力，在五个地理区域授予 20 份不定期交付、不定量合同，以支持规划、设计和施工相关服务。
其他企业级解决方案包括 https://samclerk.com/opportunity/dept-of-defense/W51EW7-26-R-A002，为七个陆军驻军提供通过竞争获得的区域建筑与维修能力，以及通过位于弗吉尼亚州尤斯蒂斯堡的野战指导办公室设立的两个SBIR III合同工具，合计上限为8亿美元，用于训练支持和人员效能基础设施。
你们表明，MICC已准备好以不同方式满足需求，”MICC司令弗雷迪·L·亚当斯准将在该司令部财年年终致辞中说。“你们帮助我们扩大了创新采办工具的使用，包括其他交易授权、小企业创新研究第三阶段途径和企业合同解决方案，这些工具帮助我们更快行动，并在最关键的地方交付能力。
除现代化之外，MICC还继续履行其对美国小企业的长期承诺，尽管面临人员削减和日益复杂的需求，仍连续第12年超额完成其被分配的小企业目标。
连续第12年全面超额完成小企业目标，是我们合同与小企业专业人员取得的非凡成就，”陆军合同司令部-MICC小企业项目办公室主任路易斯·特立尼达说。“在人员减少30%的情况下，我们的团队仍迎难而上，应对更繁重的工作量。
特立尼达说，随着合同业务在这一年增长，该司令部符合小企业条件的资金也增加了1.048亿美元，这要求对价值更高且日益复杂的采办包进行更详细的审查。
通过对每一个机会进行彻底、详细的审查，”特立尼达说，“我们的团队确保实现了所有目标，同时交付了直接支持作战人员的重要小企业能力和服务。
展望2027财年，MICC预计现代化需求将持续增长，对企业级合同解决方案的需求将增加，并将更多使用针对特定任务和士兵需求定制的创新采购授权。
MICC司令副手克莱·科尔还在收官致辞中赞扬了全体员工，称其帮助该司令部实现了与司令部《2026-2027年战役计划》相一致的重点事项，该计划强调人员与培养合同专家、战备、任务执行和转型。
科尔说：“我们共同建立了首个覆盖全机构的建筑-工程合同能力，范围遍及美国本土和波多黎各；加快了关键维持、恢复和现代化需求；并扩大了住房、营房及其他生活质量保障。
这些成就表明，当合同专业人员被赋权去创新、协作并始终聚焦作战人员时，会取得怎样的成果。
本财年收官也恰逢该合同司令部成立18周年。该机构于2008年10月1日在陆军合同司令部之下作为设施合同司令部成立，并于次日改名为MICC，如今已发展成为陆军战备和现代化的关键合同力量。
随着该司令部进入2027财年，司令部团队还强调，自成立以来取得的一长串成就，反映了其分散在各地的工作人员中合同专业人员的专业能力和奉献精神。
在短短二十年间，MICC 已发展成为陆军任务中不可或缺的一部分，而这一成就完全归功于像你们这样的专业人员的辛勤工作和卓越表现，”亚当斯说。
领导们感谢了 MICC 的工作人员和士兵，敦促他们在进入新财年之际花点时间回顾所取得的一切成就，同时保持积极势头。

关于 MICC：任务与设施合同司令部总部位于得克萨斯州圣安东尼奥联合基地-萨姆·休斯敦堡，由约1500名军人和文职人员组成，负责为支持士兵采购物资和服务，并在接到召唤时为作战部队和应急环境准备好训练有素的合同单位。作为陆军合同司令部和陆军装备司令部的下属司令部，MICC 的合同对于每天为超过20万名士兵提供膳食、在各设施提供许多日常基地运营支持服务、促进每年超过10万名常规部队成员的训练准备、每年培训超过50万名学员，以及维护超过1440万英亩土地和17万座建筑物至关重要。另请参阅 MICC 情况说明书。

得克萨斯州圣安东尼奥-萨姆休斯敦堡联合基地——任务与设施合同司令部以超过21,450项合同行动、价值约68亿美元结束2026财年，其中包括授予美国小企业的29亿美元，同时该司令部扩大了其在陆军现代化和创新采办中的作用。

该司令部还管理了超过299,000笔政府采购卡交易，价值超过5.2亿美元，为支持整个陆军的士兵、设施和任务伙伴提供了额外的购买力。

这些结果反映出合同义务比2025财年增加超过10亿美元，主要驱动因素是不断增长的设施现代化需求、扩大的采办权限，以及1月将第410合同保障旅纳入MICC的业务组合。

当我们欢迎第410合同保障旅加入该司令部时，一些增长是预料之中的，”MICC指挥军士长珍妮安妮·布赖特在MICC指挥团队10月1日致全体工作人员的信中说。

但10亿美元的增长反映了对你们专业能力日益增长的需求，以及你们在需求点向士兵和我们的任务伙伴提供合同解决方案的能力。

MICC合同运营副主任戴维·马凯尔兹将大部分增长归因于设施现代化举措，这些举措扩大了该司令部的合同职责。

新立法和更新的 https://safe.menlosecurity.com/doc/docview/viewer/docN1987DD0EE1BB421b71bea1981c758cc762275de2744473ce785c6a82335a7fe32a2649805e0e 使 MICC 能够直接支持历史上由美国陆军工程兵团管理的建设和现代化需求，”Markelz 说。该司令部通过采用更广泛的采购授权作为回应，包括其他交易授权（OTA）、小企业创新研究第三阶段（SBIR III）和多项授标任务订单（MATOC），以应对复杂、多层次的区域需求，并扩大与工业界合作的机会。

通过采用更广泛的采购授权，MICC 比以往任何时候都更有能力满足陆军不断变化的需求，并及时交付以任务为重点的成果。

年度主要成就包括设施、运营、战备、增长与经验（FORGE）倡议，这些倡议将多项现代化需求整合为更大规模、协调一致的采购工作，将相关需求打包，以交付有效成果，而不是因僵化流程而将项目割裂开来。

在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地，MICC 授予了一份价值 1.691 亿美元的其他交易协议，支持 17 个现代化项目。在阿拉巴马州安尼斯顿陆军仓库，另一项 MICC FORGE 倡议确立了约 9.87 亿美元的现代化工作，其中约 6.58 亿美元初步承付，用于支持关键军事建设和陆军有机工业基础的改进。

MICC 的其他显著工作包括一项约 2.01 亿美元的其他交易协议，用于波尔克堡轮换部队住宿区（RUBA），采用建筑规模增材制造；以及在新墨西哥州麦格雷戈靶场开展的类似约 1300 万美元 OTA 住宿工作。

MICC 还建立了其首个全企业范围的建筑-工程合同能力，在五个地理区域授予 20 份不定期交付、不定量合同，以支持规划、设计和施工相关服务。

其他企业级解决方案包括 https://samclerk.com/opportunity/dept-of-defense/W51EW7-26-R-A002，为七个陆军驻军提供通过竞争获得的区域建筑与维修能力，以及通过位于弗吉尼亚州尤斯蒂斯堡的野战指导办公室设立的两个SBIR III合同工具，合计上限为8亿美元，用于训练支持和人员效能基础设施。

你们表明，MICC已准备好以不同方式满足需求，”MICC司令弗雷迪·L·亚当斯准将在该司令部财年年终致辞中说。“你们帮助我们扩大了创新采办工具的使用，包括其他交易授权、小企业创新研究第三阶段途径和企业合同解决方案，这些工具帮助我们更快行动，并在最关键的地方交付能力。

除现代化之外，MICC还继续履行其对美国小企业的长期承诺，尽管面临人员削减和日益复杂的需求，仍连续第12年超额完成其被分配的小企业目标。

连续第12年全面超额完成小企业目标，是我们合同与小企业专业人员取得的非凡成就，”陆军合同司令部-MICC小企业项目办公室主任路易斯·特立尼达说。“在人员减少30%的情况下，我们的团队仍迎难而上，应对更繁重的工作量。

特立尼达说，随着合同业务在这一年增长，该司令部符合小企业条件的资金也增加了1.048亿美元，这要求对价值更高且日益复杂的采办包进行更详细的审查。

通过对每一个机会进行彻底、详细的审查，”特立尼达说，“我们的团队确保实现了所有目标，同时交付了直接支持作战人员的重要小企业能力和服务。

展望2027财年，MICC预计现代化需求将持续增长，对企业级合同解决方案的需求将增加，并将更多使用针对特定任务和士兵需求定制的创新采购授权。

MICC司令副手克莱·科尔还在收官致辞中赞扬了全体员工，称其帮助该司令部实现了与司令部《2026-2027年战役计划》相一致的重点事项，该计划强调人员与培养合同专家、战备、任务执行和转型。

items.body:
SAN DIEGO — Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 9 has concluded a 10-month combat deployment aboard Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72), Oct. 8. Since embarking Nov. 21, 2025, the Navy’s premier next-generation air wing served as the primary offensive power for the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group, demonstrating lethal precision during Operation Epic Fury in the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations.

Over the course of the deployment, the air wing safely completed 14,037 aircraft sorties and accumulated 31,460 forward-deployed flight hours.

Operation Epic Fury was initiated under a direct presidential order Feb. 28. In response, CVW-9 launched into a 38-day air and sea campaign to degrade Iranian power projection capabilities and defend our national interests. The air wing destroyed offensive missile sites, production facilities, military infrastructure and naval combatants before an early April ceasefire.

It expended 1,499 precision weapons, delivering over 1.37 million pounds of ordnance against U.S. Central Command priority targets, while simultaneously executing robust defensive operations to shield the strike group from attacks.

"The rapid mobilization and combat execution of CVW-9 during Operation Epic Fury demonstrated the unmatched flexibility of a U.S. Navy carrier strike group," said Navy Capt. J.W. Stigi, commander of CVW-9. "Pairing fifth-generation F-35C stealth and sensor fusion with fourth-generation workhorse strike and electronic attack platforms, Team Shogun destroyed Iran’s conventional Navy and secured vital maritime chokepoints in support of our commander’s objectives."

The integration of the F-35C Lightning II, alongside F/A-18E/F Super Hornets and EA-18G Growler electronic attack aircraft, allowed CVW-9 to penetrate highly contested airspace, proving the effectiveness of the Navy's "Air Wing of the Future" in active combat.

Despite challenges, the air wing’s maintenance professionals demonstrated outstanding self-sufficiency while operating at sea for more than 310 days.

“Our maintenance teams and aircrew sustained a relentlessly high operational tempo under demanding conditions,” said Navy Capt. Kristen Findlay, deputy commander of CVW-9. “Their performance ensured our aircraft were ready when the mission demanded it most and demonstrated that an aircraft carrier and carrier air wing remain the Navy’s premier team for generating combat power from sea.”

After 10 months of successful sustained combat operation, the Sailors and Marines of CVW-9 now shift their focus to a well-deserved period of rest, recovery and long-awaited reunions with their families.

Operating the most advanced aircraft in the U.S. inventory, CVW-9 is a next-generation, multi-platform air wing, enabling mobile naval air power projection and forward operational presence. The nine squadrons in the air wing are Marine Fighter Attack Squadron (VMFA) 314; the F/A-18 E/F Super Hornet squadrons Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 14, VFA-41 and VFA-151; Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 133; Airborne Command and Control Squadron (VAW) 117; Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 71; Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 14; and Fleet Logistics Multi-Mission Squadron (VRM) 30.

The Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group consists of flagship Abraham Lincoln, embarked staffs of Carrier Strike Group 3 and Destroyer Squadron 21, CVW-9, Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG 121) serving as the integrated air and missile defense commander, and DESRON 21’s Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers USS Spruance (DDG 111) and USS Michael Murphy (DDG 112).

Spruance and Michael Murphy remain underway in the U.S. 7th Fleet and U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations supporting global maritime security operations.
items.titleZh: 第9航母航空联队完成为期10个月的作战部署
items.summaryZh: 圣迭戈——第9航母航空联队（CVW-9）已于10月8日结束在尼米兹级航空母舰“亚伯拉罕·林肯”号（CVN 72）上为期10个月的作战部署。自2025年11月21日登舰以来，海军首屈一指的下一代航空联队作为“亚伯拉罕·林肯”号航母打击群的主要进攻力量，在美国第五舰队作战区域内“史诗狂怒行动”中展现出致命精准打击能力。在部署期间，该航空联队安全完成了14,037个飞机架次。
zhParas: 圣迭戈——第9航母航空联队（CVW-9）已于10月8日结束在尼米兹级航空母舰“亚伯拉罕·林肯”号（CVN 72）上为期10个月的作战部署。自2025年11月21日登舰以来，海军首屈一指的下一代航空联队作为“亚伯拉罕·林肯”号航母打击群的主要进攻力量，在美国第五舰队作战区域内“史诗狂怒行动”中展现出致命精准打击能力。
在部署期间，该航空联队安全完成14,037架次飞机出动，并累计前沿部署飞行小时31,460小时。
史诗狂怒行动”根据总统直接命令于2月28日启动。作为回应，第9航母航空联队发起为期38天的空海作战行动，以削弱伊朗的力量投送能力并捍卫我们的国家利益。该航空联队在4月初停火前摧毁了进攻性导弹阵地、生产设施、军事基础设施和海军作战舰艇。
该联队消耗了1,499件精确武器，向美军中央司令部优先目标投送了超过137万磅弹药，同时执行强有力的防御行动，以保护航母打击群免受攻击。
第9航母航空联队在‘史诗狂怒行动’期间的快速动员和作战执行，展现了美国海军航母打击群无与伦比的灵活性，”第9航母航空联队指挥官、海军上校J.W.斯蒂吉说。“将第五代F-35C隐身和传感器融合能力，与第四代主力打击及电子攻击平台相结合，‘幕府将军’团队摧毁了伊朗常规海军，并确保了关键海上咽喉要道，以支持我们指挥官的目标。
F-35C“闪电II”与F/A-18E/F“超级大黄蜂”以及EA-18G“咆哮者”电子攻击机的整合，使第9航母航空联队能够突入高度争夺空域，证明了海军“未来航空联队”在实战中的有效性。
尽管面临挑战，该舰载机联队的维修专业人员在海上运作超过310天期间展现出卓越的自给自足能力。
我们的维修团队和空勤人员在严苛条件下保持了持续高强度作战节奏，”第9舰载机联队（CVW-9）副指挥官、海军上校克里斯汀·芬德利说。“他们的表现确保我们的飞机在任务最需要时准备就绪，并表明航母和舰载机联队仍然是海军从海上生成战斗力的首要团队。
在成功持续进行10个月作战行动之后，第9舰载机联队（CVW-9）的水兵和海军陆战队员现在将重心转向当之无愧的休息、恢复以及与家人期盼已久的团聚时光。

items.title: Soldiers' bravery saves lives during Epic Fury
items.author: Derika Upshaw
items.summary: On the morning of March 27, the piercing sound of the “Alarm Red” warning rang out across Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia. Sgt. Xavier Jones, Staff Sgt. Kalob Mitchell and Spc. Nicholas Cabo, all with the 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, rushed to Bunker 100, expecting another missile warning. Within moments, the shelter meant to protect them would become the site of one of the most significant moments of their lives.
items.body:
On the morning of March 27, the piercing sound of the “Alarm Red” warning rang out across Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia. Sgt. Xavier Jones, Staff Sgt. Kalob Mitchell and Spc. Nicholas Cabo, all with the 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, rushed to Bunker 100, expecting another missile warning. Within moments, the shelter meant to protect them would become the site of one of the most significant moments of their lives.

Seconds later, a 550-pound ballistic missile exploded yards from the bunker’s location with overwhelming force filling it with dust and debris. Staff Sgt. Kalob Mitchell, 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, initializes the Sentinel Radar Nov. 13, 2025, at Prince Sultan Air Force Base, Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia.

“We’re sitting there talking, and then all of a sudden, we didn’t hear anything, no sound at all. Everything went black, so we were hit,” Mitchell said.

The blast wave threw them from their position and slammed them against the opposing interior wall, and in an instant, all three Soldiers lost consciousness. Staff Sgt. Kalob Mitchell, Sgt. Xavier Jones and Spc. Nicholas Cabo, all part of 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, sit together after their initial medical evaluation on March 27 at the Role 2 Medical Facility at Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia.

“I was awoken by Spc. Alma. Woke up, checked on them. They were good. At that time, we heard screams from the opposite side of the bunker. Two Soldiers, I’m not too sure who they were, who had significant injuries; ran over there, applied tourniquets, T Triple C (Tactical Combat Casualty Care), everything,” Mitchell recounted. Still dazed from the blast, Mitchell relied on instinct and training. Alongside Cabo and Jones, Mitchell applied a tourniquet to a severely wounded Soldier, treated another with a neck injury and helped calm and keep safe a disoriented Soldier until it was safe to evacuate the bunker. Staff Sgt. Kalob Mitchell, 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, poses for a picture after the Purple Heart ceremony on Oct. 1 at the III Armored Corps headquarters building at Fort Hood, to recognize him for his bravery and selfless service during a missile attack at Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia.

“Sgt. Jones and I even carried them out to the ambulance on the stretcher,” Cabo said. “So, because nobody else came in the bunker, they just brought the stretcher, and two people, and we’re like, well, someone else has to help y’all, so we carried them out.”

Despite their own injuries Mitchell, Cabo and Jones were able to help others. Sgt. Xavier Jones, the 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, poses for a picture after the Purple Heart ceremony on Oct. 1 at the III Armored Corps headquarters building at Fort Hood, to recognize him for his bravery and selfless service during a missile attack at Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia.

“I think it was just the adrenaline because after we woke up, I checked myself,” Cabo said. “I just saw that my leg was a little bit bleeding, so I didn’t really mind it. It wasn’t anything like crazy bleeding, so we just heard screams and went to go help those guys.”

Jones, Mitchell and Cabo believed that the intensive damage to the Soldier’s leg, could have cost him his life if the trio were not there. Spc. Nicholas Cabo, 6th Battalion, 56th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division Artillery, poses for a picture after the Purple Heart ceremony on Oct. 1 at the III Armored Corps headquarters building at Fort Hood, to recognize him for his bravery and selfless service during a missile attack at Prince Sultan Air Base in Al Kharj, Saudi Arabia.

“That guy probably would have died because he was bleeding a lot from his right leg, and good thing Sgt. Mitchell just came up really quick, then called for us and we helped him out,” Cabo said.

Capt. Tyler Ritter, commander of 6-56 ADAR, 1st Cav. DIVARTY, received messages from the injured Soldier saying, “Sir, your Soldiers saved my life. I thank God every day that these gentlemen survived. Their actions brought great credit upon the 6-56 Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division and III Armored Corps. These Soldiers are my heroes. May God bless them.”

This selfless service, a pillar of the Army values, earned each of the three Soldiers the Purple Heart medal — approved by the Department of the Army July 17, followed by a recognition ceremony on Oct. 1. Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral, III Armored Corps and Fort Hood commanding general, described the act as the “ultimate description of what we mean when we talk about warfighting, readiness, grit and taking care of our Soldiers.”

Mitchell, Cabo and Jones said they were grateful to receive the recognition.

“So honestly, it’s kind of cool,” Jones said. “I don’t think any of us was like going for a Purple Heart because it actually sucked. Like that situation was horrible … When I saw it on my STP (Soldier Talent Profile) I was like man, I never would have thought I would have got a Purple Heart. I never thought I was going to see anything like we saw.”

Mitchell said he was just glad they are still here to tell the story and to pass on to those who have not seen any combat that what they are doing matters. The solace Mitchell takes in the realization that they almost died is overwhelming, he explained.

“The one that hit us was on the smaller side, so it was about 250 kilograms of explosive versus what some of the bigger ones they had hit us with, which were about 750,” Mitchell said. “And all it would have took was it being one of those, and we wouldn’t have been here.

“I guess I’d say that it kind of puts it in perspective that we went, we did our job to the best of our ability and we almost paid the ultimate price,” Mitchell added.

Mitchell urges other Soldiers to hone in on their skills, or whatever their profession is, because one day they may be called to show up and put them to use.

The trio agreed that the long hours in the field for training can be relentless, however, it is critically important. “I think that’s probably the biggest thing about the Army that’s annoying because you don’t get that real feeling all the time, so when you’re out in the field and it kind of seems pointless … you’re just like ‘why are we doing this?’ And then once you actually do it, like it was definitely beneficial,” Jones said.

Mitchell said he feels they do not appreciate the importance of field exercises until they experience something like Operation Epic Fury and those skills came in handy.

“I know it sucks going to the field and all that, but it gets you ready,” Mitchell said. “So, when I was putting the tourniquet and everything on, like, the shell shock was real. I was on autopilot. I had no idea where I was, what I was doing, but I’d done it so many times, putting on a tourniquet. It was like second nature for me.”

Mitchell did such a good job with the tourniquet; the surgeon said she thought one of the paramedics had put it on.

Though the trio felt great about saving lives, the journey back home was not easy and they were grateful for the resources at their disposal. Cabo explained he went between three different hospitals from Germany to Virginia, then Fort Hood, passing medical notes from each visit through the system.

“All those notes came down, and with the Intrepid Center, they are all trying to help to reintegrate, but there’s just so much that they need to do in so little time that all these appointments, plus trying to do regular work, both were a little bit stressful,” he said.

The Soldiers also recognized the struggle of leaving a deployed site to come back to garrison. Jones noticed the difference in the need to fix equipment there versus fixing it here at home.

“I’m trying to get back to reality, trying to get anxiety back down, trying to just not be as alert, trying to reintegrate,” Jones said. “I was at work a couple of weeks before I took leave, and it just was ... it felt different. Like it felt non-serious, and it just was throwing me off because seeing everybody have fun, we had fun too, but … it was just different.”

Jones shared on a more personal level, they were suffering while just trying to get back to a “garrison” state. The Soldiers attest to sleeping problems and moments of antisocial behavior.

“So I guess it has this ... like a slight impact because I just don’t want to be around people,” Jones said. “I mean, I’m a gamer initially, but I usually try to go out. But now I don’t even try to go. I really just chill.”

Cabo has also had his moments.

“Because there’s the runway, the airfield runway over there. So, one day I went to Sam’s Club, and I was like, ‘oh, drone’, and so I stopped and looked. I’m like, ‘it’s coming.’ Then I saw the plane, or the type of aircraft it was, I was like, ‘oh crap, it’s just in my head.’”

While reintegration has presented its challenges, the Soldiers said support from family, friends and behavioral health professionals has played a vital role in helping them adapt and heal.

“I find it super helpful because the only person I would talk to about the situation, if anyone, besides like behavioral health, will just either be the team or my wife. So talking to somebody who has an outside perspective from it is good,” Cabo said.

Cabo urges other Soldiers to do the same.

“Just go to appointments and try to really give them (medical professionals) honest feedback so they can help you as much as they can and give you what you really need,” Cabo said.

Mitchell agreed. “I feel like it’s, kind of, instilled in the military, like don’t go to sick call. Like, you’ll be seen as a problem child. Like they’re running from something. But these are real issues, and they need to be addressed. So be honest with the medical staff and get the help you need,” Mitchell said.

Although the past several months have tested them physically and emotionally, the trio’s bond remains strong. They still find reasons to laugh together, balancing lighthearted moments with honest conversations about their shared experiences.

Jones said the ceremony went beyond what was necessary. For him, a high-five would have sufficed.

"I mean, we raised our right hand for a reason," Jones said. "We all knew what we were going into."

Without a family military background, he enlisted to serve his country and support his daughter, never expecting public recognition. To him, the occasional ‘thank you for your service’ was all the acknowledgment he would receive.

For those struggling with reintegration, Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center programs such as the Multi-D Behavioral Clinic and Outpatient Behavioral Health clinic, which accepts walk-ins, can help. Call 254-553-3624 or 254-553-8711.
items.titleZh: 士兵的英勇在“史诗之怒”期间拯救生命
items.summaryZh: 3月27日早晨，刺耳的“红色警报”警告声响彻沙特阿拉伯海尔季的苏尔坦亲王空军基地。均隶属于第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的中士泽维尔·琼斯、上士卡洛布·米切尔和技术兵尼古拉斯·卡博冲向100号掩体，以为又是一次导弹警报。片刻之间，这座本应用来保护他们的掩体，将成为他们人生中最重要时刻之一的现场。
zhParas: 3月27日早晨，刺耳的“红色警报”警告声响彻沙特阿拉伯海尔季的苏尔坦亲王空军基地。均隶属于第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的中士泽维尔·琼斯、上士卡洛布·米切尔和技术兵尼古拉斯·卡博冲向100号掩体，以为又是一次导弹警报。片刻之间，这座本应用来保护他们的掩体，将成为他们人生中最重要时刻之一的现场。
几秒钟后，一枚550磅重的弹道导弹在距掩体位置数码处爆炸，以巨大的威力使掩体内满是尘土和碎片。2025年11月13日，第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营上士卡洛布·米切尔在沙特阿拉伯海尔季的苏尔坦亲王空军基地启动“哨兵”雷达。
我们正坐在那里说话，然后突然间，我们什么都听不到了，一点声音都没有。眼前一黑，所以我们被击中了，”米切尔说。
爆炸冲击波把他们从所在位置掀飞，猛撞到对面的内墙上，瞬间，三名士兵全部失去意识。3月27日，在沙特阿拉伯海尔季的苏尔坦亲王空军基地二级医疗设施接受初步医疗评估后，均隶属于第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的上士卡洛布·米切尔、中士泽维尔·琼斯和技术兵尼古拉斯·卡博坐在一起。

我被技术兵阿尔玛叫醒。醒来后，我查看了他们的情况。他们没事。那时，我们听到掩体对面传来尖叫声。有两名士兵——我不太确定他们是谁——受了重伤；我跑过去，给他们扎止血带，进行T Triple C（战术战伤救治），能做的都做了，”米切尔回忆道。仍被爆炸震得头晕目眩的米切尔依靠本能和训练行动。米切尔与卡博和琼斯一道，为一名重伤士兵扎上止血带，救治另一名颈部受伤的士兵，并帮助安抚和保护一名神志不清的士兵，直到可以安全撤离掩体。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行的紫心勋章授勋仪式后，第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营上士卡洛布·米切尔合影留念；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏尔坦亲王空军基地遭导弹袭击期间表现出的勇敢和无私服务。
琼斯中士和我甚至用担架把他们抬到了救护车上，”卡博说。“因为没有人再进掩体，他们只带来了担架和两个人，我们就想，得有人帮你们一把，于是我们把他们抬了出去。
尽管米切尔、卡博和琼斯自己也受了伤，他们仍能帮助其他人。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行紫心勋章颁授仪式后，来自第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的泽维尔·琼斯中士留影；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏丹王子空军基地遭导弹袭击期间的勇敢和无私服务。
我觉得那只是肾上腺素的作用，因为我们醒来后，我检查了自己，”卡博说。“我只看到腿有点流血，所以没太在意。并不是那种疯狂流血，所以我们只听到尖叫声，就过去帮那些人。
琼斯、米切尔和卡博认为，如果不是他们三人在场，那名士兵腿部的严重损伤本可能让他丧命。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行紫心勋章颁授仪式后，来自第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的技术兵尼古拉斯·卡博留影；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏丹王子空军基地遭导弹袭击期间的勇敢和无私服务。
那个家伙当时可能已经没命了，因为他的右腿流了很多血，幸好米切尔中士很快赶了过来，然后叫上我们，我们一起帮了他，”卡博说。
第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营指挥官泰勒·里特上尉收到了那名受伤士兵发来的信息，写道：“长官，您的士兵救了我的命。我每天都感谢上帝，让这些先生们活了下来。他们的行动为第56防空炮兵团第6营、第1骑兵师和第3装甲军带来了巨大荣誉。这些士兵是我的英雄。愿上帝保佑他们。
这种无私服务是陆军价值观的支柱之一，使这三名士兵每人都获得了紫心勋章——该勋章于7月17日获陆军部批准，随后于10月1日举行了表彰仪式。第3装甲军兼胡德堡司令官凯文·D·阿德默中将称这一行为是“对我们谈到作战、战备、坚毅和关爱士兵时所指含义的终极诠释”。
米切尔、卡波和琼斯表示，他们很感激获得这一认可。
所以老实说，这还挺酷的，”琼斯说。“我不认为我们中有谁是为了紫心勋章才去的，因为这玩意儿其实糟透了。那个情况太可怕了……当我在我的STP（士兵人才档案）上看到它时，我心想，天哪，我从没想到自己会获得紫心勋章。我从没想到会看到我们所看到的那种场面。
米切尔说，他只是很高兴他们还在这里讲述这个故事，并告诉那些从未见过战斗的人，他们所做的一切很重要。米切尔解释说，他从他们险些丧命这一认识中获得的慰藉是巨大的。
击中我们的那一枚算是较小的，大约有250公斤炸药，而他们击中我们的那些更大的约有750公斤，”米切尔说。“只要击中我们的是那种大的，我们就不会还在这里了。
我想我会说，这让人更清楚地认识到，我们去了，我们尽了最大能力履行职责，而且我们差点付出了终极代价，”米切尔补充说。
米切尔敦促其他士兵磨炼自己的技能，或者无论他们的专业是什么，因为总有一天他们可能会被召去到场并把这些技能派上用场。
三人一致认为，在野外进行长时间训练可能十分艰苦，但这至关重要。“我认为这大概是陆军最让人烦的一点，因为你并不是总能获得那种真实的感觉；所以当你身处野外，而这件事看起来有点毫无意义时……你就会想‘我们为什么要这么做？’可一旦你真的这么做了，就会发现它绝对是有益的，”琼斯说。
米切尔说，他觉得直到他们经历像“史诗之怒行动”这样的事情、那些技能派上用场时，他们才会真正体会到野外演习的重要性。
我知道去野外什么的很糟糕，但它能让你做好准备，”米切尔说。“所以，当我在缠止血带、处理那些事的时候，那种弹震症是真实存在的。我当时处于自动驾驶状态。我不知道自己在哪里，在做什么，但我已经做过很多次缠止血带了。这对我来说就像第二天性。
米切尔止血带处理得非常好，外科医生说她还以为是一名急救员扎上的。
尽管三人对挽救了生命感到非常欣慰，但回国之路并不轻松，他们对可支配的资源心怀感激。卡博解释说，他从德国到弗吉尼亚，再到胡德堡，辗转于三家不同的医院，并通过系统传递每次就诊的医疗记录。
所有这些病历都传了下来，而无畏中心这边，他们都在努力帮助我重新融入，但他们需要在这么短的时间里做这么多事，所有这些预约，再加上还要努力完成日常工作，这两方面都让人有点压力，”他说。
士兵们也体会到了离开部署地点、返回驻防地的艰难。琼斯注意到，在那里维修装备与在国内这里维修装备的需求有所不同。
我正试着回归现实，试着让焦虑平复下来，试着不那么高度警觉，试着重新融入，”琼斯说。“我在休假前上了几周班，可就是……感觉不一样。就好像一切变得不严肃，这让我很不适应，因为看到每个人都在开心，我们也开心过，但……就是不一样。
琼斯更个人化地分享说，他们仅仅为了恢复到“驻防”状态就在受苦。这些士兵证实，他们存在睡眠问题，也会出现一些不合群的时刻。
所以我想这……有点影响，因为我就是不想和人待在一起，”琼斯说。“我的意思是，我本来是个游戏玩家，但通常我会尽量出门。可现在我都懒得尝试出门。我真的就只是放松待着。
卡博也有过类似的时刻。
因为那边有跑道，机场跑道。所以有一天我去山姆会员商店，当时就想，‘哦，无人机’，于是我停下来看。我心想，‘它来了。’然后我看到了那架飞机，或者说看清了它是什么类型的飞机，我就想，‘哦，糟了，这只是我脑子里瞎想的。’
尽管重新融入带来了挑战，但士兵们表示，来自家人、朋友和行为健康专业人员的支持在帮助他们适应和康复方面发挥了至关重要的作用。
我觉得这非常有帮助，因为除了行为健康人员之外，如果有谁能让我谈谈这件事，那要么是我的团队，要么是我妻子。所以，和一个能从外部视角看待这件事的人聊聊是件好事，”卡波说。
卡波敦促其他士兵也这样做。
就去赴诊，尽量如实向（医疗专业人员）反馈，这样他们才能尽可能帮助你，并给你真正需要的东西，”卡波说。
米切尔对此表示同意。“我觉得军队里多少灌输了一种观念，比如不要去医务所看病。否则你会被视为问题人物，好像你在逃避什么。但这些都是真实存在的问题，需要得到解决。所以，对医务人员坦诚，并获得你需要的帮助，”米切尔说。
尽管过去几个月在身体和情感上都考验了他们，但三人的纽带依然牢固。他们仍然能找到一起开怀大笑的理由，在轻松时刻与围绕共同经历的坦诚交谈之间保持平衡。
琼斯说，这场仪式超出了必要程度。对他来说，一个击掌本已足够。
我的意思是，我们举起右手宣誓是有原因的，”琼斯说。“我们都清楚自己将面对什么。
由于没有军人家庭背景，他入伍是为了报效国家并供养女儿，从未指望获得公众认可。对他而言，偶尔听到一句‘感谢你的服役’便是他能得到的全部认可。
对于在重新融入方面有困难的人，卡尔·R·达纳尔陆军医疗中心的项目可以提供帮助，例如多学科行为诊所和接受无需预约就诊的门诊行为健康诊所。请致电 254-553-3624 或 254-553-8711。

我们正坐在那里说话，然后突然间，我们什么都听不到了，一点声音都没有。眼前一黑，所以我们被击中了，”米切尔说。

我被技术兵阿尔玛叫醒。醒来后，我查看了他们的情况。他们没事。那时，我们听到掩体对面传来尖叫声。有两名士兵——我不太确定他们是谁——受了重伤；我跑过去，给他们扎止血带，进行T Triple C（战术战伤救治），能做的都做了，”米切尔回忆道。仍被爆炸震得头晕目眩的米切尔依靠本能和训练行动。米切尔与卡博和琼斯一道，为一名重伤士兵扎上止血带，救治另一名颈部受伤的士兵，并帮助安抚和保护一名神志不清的士兵，直到可以安全撤离掩体。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行的紫心勋章授勋仪式后，第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营上士卡洛布·米切尔合影留念；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏尔坦亲王空军基地遭导弹袭击期间表现出的勇敢和无私服务。

琼斯中士和我甚至用担架把他们抬到了救护车上，”卡博说。“因为没有人再进掩体，他们只带来了担架和两个人，我们就想，得有人帮你们一把，于是我们把他们抬了出去。

尽管米切尔、卡博和琼斯自己也受了伤，他们仍能帮助其他人。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行紫心勋章颁授仪式后，来自第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的泽维尔·琼斯中士留影；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏丹王子空军基地遭导弹袭击期间的勇敢和无私服务。

我觉得那只是肾上腺素的作用，因为我们醒来后，我检查了自己，”卡博说。“我只看到腿有点流血，所以没太在意。并不是那种疯狂流血，所以我们只听到尖叫声，就过去帮那些人。

琼斯、米切尔和卡博认为，如果不是他们三人在场，那名士兵腿部的严重损伤本可能让他丧命。10月1日，在胡德堡第3装甲军总部大楼举行紫心勋章颁授仪式后，来自第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营的技术兵尼古拉斯·卡博留影；该仪式旨在表彰他在沙特阿拉伯海尔季苏丹王子空军基地遭导弹袭击期间的勇敢和无私服务。

那个家伙当时可能已经没命了，因为他的右腿流了很多血，幸好米切尔中士很快赶了过来，然后叫上我们，我们一起帮了他，”卡博说。

第1骑兵师炮兵第56防空炮兵团第6营指挥官泰勒·里特上尉收到了那名受伤士兵发来的信息，写道：“长官，您的士兵救了我的命。我每天都感谢上帝，让这些先生们活了下来。他们的行动为第56防空炮兵团第6营、第1骑兵师和第3装甲军带来了巨大荣誉。这些士兵是我的英雄。愿上帝保佑他们。

这种无私服务是陆军价值观的支柱之一，使这三名士兵每人都获得了紫心勋章——该勋章于7月17日获陆军部批准，随后于10月1日举行了表彰仪式。第3装甲军兼胡德堡司令官凯文·D·阿德默中将称这一行为是“对我们谈到作战、战备、坚毅和关爱士兵时所指含义的终极诠释”。

米切尔、卡波和琼斯表示，他们很感激获得这一认可。

所以老实说，这还挺酷的，”琼斯说。“我不认为我们中有谁是为了紫心勋章才去的，因为这玩意儿其实糟透了。那个情况太可怕了……当我在我的STP（士兵人才档案）上看到它时，我心想，天哪，我从没想到自己会获得紫心勋章。我从没想到会看到我们所看到的那种场面。

米切尔说，他只是很高兴他们还在这里讲述这个故事，并告诉那些从未见过战斗的人，他们所做的一切很重要。米切尔解释说，他从他们险些丧命这一认识中获得的慰藉是巨大的。

击中我们的那一枚算是较小的，大约有250公斤炸药，而他们击中我们的那些更大的约有750公斤，”米切尔说。“只要击中我们的是那种大的，我们就不会还在这里了。

我想我会说，这让人更清楚地认识到，我们去了，我们尽了最大能力履行职责，而且我们差点付出了终极代价，”米切尔补充说。

米切尔敦促其他士兵磨炼自己的技能，或者无论他们的专业是什么，因为总有一天他们可能会被召去到场并把这些技能派上用场。

三人一致认为，在野外进行长时间训练可能十分艰苦，但这至关重要。“我认为这大概是陆军最让人烦的一点，因为你并不是总能获得那种真实的感觉；所以当你身处野外，而这件事看起来有点毫无意义时……你就会想‘我们为什么要这么做？’可一旦你真的这么做了，就会发现它绝对是有益的，”琼斯说。

米切尔说，他觉得直到他们经历像“史诗之怒行动”这样的事情、那些技能派上用场时，他们才会真正体会到野外演习的重要性。

我知道去野外什么的很糟糕，但它能让你做好准备，”米切尔说。“所以，当我在缠止血带、处理那些事的时候，那种弹震症是真实存在的。我当时处于自动驾驶状态。我不知道自己在哪里，在做什么，但我已经做过很多次缠止血带了。这对我来说就像第二天性。

米切尔止血带处理得非常好，外科医生说她还以为是一名急救员扎上的。

尽管三人对挽救了生命感到非常欣慰，但回国之路并不轻松，他们对可支配的资源心怀感激。卡博解释说，他从德国到弗吉尼亚，再到胡德堡，辗转于三家不同的医院，并通过系统传递每次就诊的医疗记录。

所有这些病历都传了下来，而无畏中心这边，他们都在努力帮助我重新融入，但他们需要在这么短的时间里做这么多事，所有这些预约，再加上还要努力完成日常工作，这两方面都让人有点压力，”他说。

士兵们也体会到了离开部署地点、返回驻防地的艰难。琼斯注意到，在那里维修装备与在国内这里维修装备的需求有所不同。

我正试着回归现实，试着让焦虑平复下来，试着不那么高度警觉，试着重新融入，”琼斯说。“我在休假前上了几周班，可就是……感觉不一样。就好像一切变得不严肃，这让我很不适应，因为看到每个人都在开心，我们也开心过，但……就是不一样。

琼斯更个人化地分享说，他们仅仅为了恢复到“驻防”状态就在受苦。这些士兵证实，他们存在睡眠问题，也会出现一些不合群的时刻。

所以我想这……有点影响，因为我就是不想和人待在一起，”琼斯说。“我的意思是，我本来是个游戏玩家，但通常我会尽量出门。可现在我都懒得尝试出门。我真的就只是放松待着。

卡博也有过类似的时刻。

因为那边有跑道，机场跑道。所以有一天我去山姆会员商店，当时就想，‘哦，无人机’，于是我停下来看。我心想，‘它来了。’然后我看到了那架飞机，或者说看清了它是什么类型的飞机，我就想，‘哦，糟了，这只是我脑子里瞎想的。’

尽管重新融入带来了挑战，但士兵们表示，来自家人、朋友和行为健康专业人员的支持在帮助他们适应和康复方面发挥了至关重要的作用。

我觉得这非常有帮助，因为除了行为健康人员之外，如果有谁能让我谈谈这件事，那要么是我的团队，要么是我妻子。所以，和一个能从外部视角看待这件事的人聊聊是件好事，”卡波说。

卡波敦促其他士兵也这样做。

就去赴诊，尽量如实向（医疗专业人员）反馈，这样他们才能尽可能帮助你，并给你真正需要的东西，”卡波说。

米切尔对此表示同意。“我觉得军队里多少灌输了一种观念，比如不要去医务所看病。否则你会被视为问题人物，好像你在逃避什么。但这些都是真实存在的问题，需要得到解决。所以，对医务人员坦诚，并获得你需要的帮助，”米切尔说。

尽管过去几个月在身体和情感上都考验了他们，但三人的纽带依然牢固。他们仍然能找到一起开怀大笑的理由，在轻松时刻与围绕共同经历的坦诚交谈之间保持平衡。

琼斯说，这场仪式超出了必要程度。对他来说，一个击掌本已足够。

我的意思是，我们举起右手宣誓是有原因的，”琼斯说。“我们都清楚自己将面对什么。

由于没有军人家庭背景，他入伍是为了报效国家并供养女儿，从未指望获得公众认可。对他而言，偶尔听到一句‘感谢你的服役’便是他能得到的全部认可。

对于在重新融入方面有困难的人，卡尔·R·达纳尔陆军医疗中心的项目可以提供帮助，例如多学科行为诊所和接受无需预约就诊的门诊行为健康诊所。请致电 254-553-3624 或 254-553-8711。

items.title: NETCOM Lunch and Learn explores multi-agent approach to SI-assisted development
items.author: Gabriel Archer
items.summary: The U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command’s (NETCOM) Data Science Directorate (DSD) held a Lunch and Learn session to demonstrate how super intelligence (SI) tools could help develop applications and address challenges across the Army enterprise.
items.body:
FORT HUACHUCA, AZ — The U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command’s (NETCOM) Data Science Directorate (DSD) held a Lunch and Learn session to demonstrate how super intelligence (SI) tools could help develop applications and address challenges across the Army enterprise.

During the session, Maj. Nolan Campbell, data scientist from DSD, showcased a method for using a SI-enabled application in the Maven Foundry environment to support product development. The process Campbell described combines an SI agent with a team of subagents to assist with tasks such as data transformations and ontology development, helping users rapidly move from requirements toward a working product.

The demonstration used a simple example: a data set of two numbers and a dashboard designed to add them. The basic use case gave attendees a way to follow the development process, while illustrating a method that could be adapted for more complex projects.

The focus was not simply on what the tools can do, but on how people can guide and combine them in different ways. That human direction, the session emphasized, can make SI use more robust, expansive and empowering.

“This isn’t just a new feature or tool demonstration,” said Patrick Goodman, NETCOM DSD Business Operations Analysis Division Chief. Goodman described the approach as a potentially significant way for the directorate and command to develop and improve applications and solve problems across NETCOM and the Army.

Campbell emphasized that the process still requires deliberate user involvement. “This is not a deterministic system by any means,” Campbell further elaborated, “there’s a lot of revision that you have to work through to guide it, but it’s still faster than manually coding something.”

The method was developed through hands-on experimentation, including testing different ways to prompt the system and direct its work. The session encouraged attendees to consider how the approach could support their own projects.

The directorate’s broader goals include unifying the Army enterprise network around zero-trust principles, building the team, sustaining network readiness, and modernizing and evolving capabilities.

Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM) is a 2-star operational command with global responsibility in constant competition, crisis, and conflict. We are responsible for providing the U.S. Army with a Unified Network based on Zero Trust Principles. We operate, maintain, and secure the Army’s portion of the Department of War Information Network through four lines of effort: assure the network, build the team, sustain network readiness, and modernize and evolve. The NETCOM team is composed of 12,000 Soldiers, Department of the Army Civilians, Host-Nation, and Contract Employees who are stationed in more than 30 countries around the world.

Voice of the Army!
items.titleZh: 美国陆军网络企业技术司令部（NETCOM）午餐学习会探讨SI辅助开发的多智能体方法
items.summaryZh: 美国陆军网络企业技术司令部（NETCOM）数据科学局（DSD）举行了一场午餐学习会，演示超级智能（SI）工具如何帮助开发应用程序并应对整个陆军企业范围面临的挑战。
zhParas: 亚利桑那州华楚卡堡——美国陆军网络企业技术司令部（NETCOM）数据科学局（DSD）举行了一场午餐学习会，演示超级智能（SI）工具如何帮助开发应用程序并应对整个陆军企业范围面临的挑战。
在会议期间，来自DSD的数据科学家诺兰·坎贝尔少校展示了一种在Maven Foundry环境中使用由超级智能赋能的应用程序来支持产品开发的方法。坎贝尔描述的这一流程将一个超级智能代理与一个子代理团队相结合，以协助完成数据转换和本体开发等任务，帮助用户迅速从需求推进到可运行的产品。
演示使用了一个简单示例：一个包含两个数字的数据集，以及一个旨在将它们相加的仪表板。这个基本用例让与会者能够跟随开发过程，同时说明了一种可适用于更复杂项目的方法。
重点不只是这些工具能做什么，还在于人们如何以不同方式引导和组合它们。会议强调，这种人工指导可以让超级智能的使用更稳健、更广泛，并更具赋能作用。
这不仅仅是一个新功能或工具的演示，”NETCOM DSD业务运营分析处处长帕特里克·古德曼说。古德曼称，这种方法可能是一种重要途径，可让该局和司令部开发并改进应用程序，并解决NETCOM和陆军范围内的问题。
坎贝尔强调，这一流程仍然需要用户有意识地参与。“这绝不是一个确定性系统，”坎贝尔进一步解释道，“你必须经过大量修订来引导它，但它仍然比手动编写代码更快。
该方法是通过动手实验开发出来的，包括测试以不同方式向系统提供提示并指导其工作。此次会议鼓励与会者思考该方法可如何支持他们自己的项目。
该局更广泛的目标包括围绕零信任原则统一陆军企业网络、建设团队、保持网络战备，以及实现能力现代化和演进。
网络企业技术司令部（NETCOM）是一个两星作战司令部，在持续竞争、危机和冲突中承担全球责任。我们负责为美国陆军提供基于零信任原则的统一网络。我们通过四条工作路线运营、维护并保护战争部信息网络中的陆军部分：保障网络、建设团队、保持网络战备以及现代化与演进。NETCOM团队由12,000名士兵、陆军部文职人员、东道国人员和合同雇员组成，他们驻扎在全球30多个国家。
陆军之声！
