items.body:
In 2007, Rafael Cervantes Jr. walked into a Marine Corps recruiting office with a friend who had recently taken the Oath to serve. Simply running errands in California alongside his friend, he had no interest in enlisting.

While making small talk with someone in the office, Cervantes was asked if he would ever join. He answered with a sincere “no.” Their response changed everything.

“Yeah, you probably couldn’t be a Marine,” they said.

Eighteen years later, 1st Sgt. Cervantes is serving as the senior enlisted advisor of USMEPCOM 11th Battalion and St. Louis MEPS. For him, that responsibility is about far more than processing applicants. It is about helping people see what they are capable of becoming.

Four years after enlisting, Cervantes was wounded when he was struck by an explosion while serving in Afghanistan. His injuries included broken feet, a broken back and pelvis, a compound fracture, hip injuries and a brain injury. He also battled a serious infection in his right ankle and spent three years as a wounded warrior.

“You get one life,” Cervantes said. “And I think there’s a reason why I’m still alive. There’s a reason why every single one of us still wakes up every day.”

He remembers those who never had the opportunity to return home, or who lost the ability to walk. For Cervantes, those realities provide perspective every day.

“I have four beautiful daughters that look at me and they think of me as a role model, as a father, as a friend,” he said. “How do I stay the healthiest possible, to have the best life possible, to be around and give them all the love they possibly need?”

His Purple Heart is a visible reminder of what he has endured, but he refuses to let his injuries define what he can do. That philosophy is at the center of the advice he gives young service members.

“Never give up,” Cervantes said. “Whatever goal you have, keep pushing for it. There’s nothing that other people can do to stop you. You just gotta go out there and do it.”

Even after his injuries, Cervantes wanted to remain in the Marine Corps. He saw staying in as an opportunity to continue helping people.His leadership philosophy is straightforward: help people make better decisions rather than simply giving them answers. It is about giving people enough perspective to make their own decisions.

That approach has extended beyond St. Louis MEPS. Cervantes has also been selected as a mentor for new commanders and senior enlisted advisors, giving him another avenue to pass along the lessons he has accumulated throughout his career. The leaders he mentors today will eventually influence their own organizations and people.

Cervantes believes MEPS personnel have an obligation to remember what is at stake for the people they serve. Some applicants may arrive carrying circumstances that are difficult for those on the other side of the desk to see.

“Some of these kids, they live in a rough neighborhood, they live in a rough situation and are under so much pressure,” Cervantes said. “Sometimes the military is the only way out. If they want to join the military, we should do everything in our power to help them through that process.”

Cervantes has seen the influence of service play out in his own family. As the oldest of four brothers and one sister, Cervantes learned early that taking care of others was part of his responsibility.

“My mother was a single woman raising us, and I was the oldest,” he said. “So as the biggest, I always had to take care of my siblings.”

When his younger brother, Luis, who was born right before Rafael enlisted, decided to join the Marine Corps, Cervantes was surprised. He had pushed his other brother toward military service in the past and he believes that pressure created resentment. With Luis, he deliberately took a different approach.

Instead, Luis spent summers with Cervantes, going to the lake and river and staying at his house.

“I think for him, he just saw a different life,” Cervantes said.

Eventually, Luis made the decision on his own. Cervantes was there when his brother earned the Eagle, Globe and Anchor atop a mountain in California. Standing among roughly 250 new Marines, Cervantes could barely recognize the person he was looking for.

“I just couldn’t believe that was him,” he said. “I was looking at my little brother, but it was a grown man. I don’t think I’ve ever been squeezed by any human being in my life that hard.”

As they walked down the mountain, Luis could have stayed beside his brother and enjoyed the moment. Instead, he stopped to help another new Marine struggling with his pack. For Cervantes, that was the real measure of his brother’s transformation.

“I probably felt the most accomplished,” he said. “To see my brother say, ‘I’m not going to be selfish and stay here and talk to you,’ even though he could have.”

Following a hip replacement, Cervantes found another place to mentor young people. Before his injuries, soccer was an important part of his life. The surgery gave him the ability to play again. He started coaching and then shifted to refereeing.

“There’s zero problems on the field,” he said. “Nothing else matters for 90 minutes. Whatever pain, depression or anxiety I have goes away.”

Cervantes referees youth, high school, college and academy-level soccer, giving him another opportunity to encourage young people who are learning how to compete, overcome setbacks and grow.

“You get to see these kids grow up, you get to see these kids evolve and make better decisions,” he said. “You get to mentor them, talk to them and push them.”

He sees refereeing as a possible professional career someday and even dreams of becoming a professional referee with a Purple Heart, a distinction he has not seen before.

After 18 years in uniform, Cervantes knows his generation will eventually have to hand the reins to the next one. He believes today’s young people have access to information, technology and resources that can help them become stronger and more capable. His responsibility, he said, is to make sure they have the tools to use those advantages. That includes teaching them something he believes is more important than any technical skill.

“You don’t have to change who you are to be successful in life,” he said. “You just gotta be a good person. Sometimes calling someone by their name, giving them a genuine compliment – you can change their life, because you never know what people are going through.”

Whether he is mentoring a new senior leader, encouraging an applicant, watching his younger brother become a Marine or standing at midfield with a whistle in his hand, Cervantes continues to help others move forward and encourages them to never let a setback decide what comes next.
items.titleZh: 紫心勋章，一生服役
items.summaryZh: 2007年，小拉斐尔·塞万提斯和一位不久前宣誓服役的朋友一起走进海军陆战队招募办公室。他当时只是陪朋友在加利福尼亚办事，对入伍毫无兴趣。在办公室里与人闲聊时，塞万提斯被问到是否会参军。他诚恳地回答“不会”。他们的回应改变了一切。“是啊，你大概当不了海军陆战队员，”他们说。十八年后，一级军士长塞万提斯正担任……
zhParas: 2007年，小拉斐尔·塞万提斯和一位不久前宣誓服役的朋友一起走进海军陆战队招募办公室。他当时只是陪朋友在加利福尼亚办事，对入伍毫无兴趣。
在办公室与某人闲聊时，有人问塞万提斯是否有一天会参军。他真诚地回答：“不会。”而他们的回应改变了一切。
是啊，你大概当不了海军陆战队员，”他们说。
十八年后，一等军士塞万提斯担任美国军事入伍处理司令部（USMEPCOM）第11营和圣路易斯军事入伍处理站（MEPS）的高级士兵顾问。对他而言，这一职责远不止处理申请人事务。它关乎帮助人们看到自己能够成为什么样的人。
入伍四年后，塞万提斯在阿富汗服役时遭遇爆炸负伤。他的伤情包括双脚骨折、背部与骨盆骨折、开放性骨折、髋部受伤以及脑损伤。他还与右脚踝的严重感染作斗争，并作为负伤勇士度过了三年。
你只有一条命，”塞万提斯说。“而且我认为，我仍然活着是有原因的。我们每一个人每天还能醒来，也是有原因的。
他铭记那些从未有机会回家的人，以及那些失去行走能力的人。对塞万提斯而言，这些现实每天都让他对人生有更清醒的认识。
我有四个美丽的女儿，她们看着我，把我视为榜样、父亲和朋友，”他说。“我该如何尽可能保持健康，尽可能拥有最好的生活，陪伴在她们身边，并给予她们可能需要的所有爱？
他的紫心勋章是他所承受一切的醒目提醒，但他拒绝让伤病界定自己能做到什么。这一理念正是他给年轻军人建议的核心。
永不放弃，”塞万提斯说。“无论你有什么目标，都要不断为之努力。别人无法阻止你。你只需要走出去，付诸行动。
即使受伤之后，塞万提斯仍想留在海军陆战队。他把继续服役视为一个继续帮助他人的机会。他的领导理念简单直接：帮助人们做出更好的决定，而不是仅仅给出答案。关键在于给人们足够的视角，让他们自己做出决定。
这种方法已经超出了圣路易斯军事入口处理站的范围。塞万提斯还被选为新任指挥官和高级士官顾问的导师，这为他提供了另一条途径，来传承他整个职业生涯中积累的经验教训。他今天指导的领导者，最终将影响他们自己的组织和人员。
塞万提斯认为，军事入伍处理站（MEPS）人员有义务记住，他们所服务的人正面临着怎样的利害关系。有些应征者来到时，可能背负着坐在桌子另一边的人难以看清的处境。
这些孩子中，有些人生活在治安很差的社区，处境艰难，承受着巨大压力，”塞万提斯说。“有时，参军是唯一的出路。如果他们想参军，我们就应该尽一切努力帮助他们完成这一过程。
塞万提斯在自己的家庭中看到了服役带来的影响。作为四个兄弟和一个姐妹中的老大，塞万提斯从小就明白，照顾他人是他责任的一部分。
我母亲是独自一人把我们抚养长大的女性，而我是老大，”他说。“所以作为最大的孩子，我一直得照顾我的弟弟妹妹。
当他的弟弟路易斯——就在拉斐尔入伍前不久出生——决定加入海军陆战队时，塞万提斯很惊讶。他过去曾推动另一个弟弟参军，并认为那种压力造成了怨恨。对路易斯，他有意采取了不同的方式。
相反，路易斯在暑假期间与塞万提斯待在一起，去湖边和河边，还住在他家里。
我觉得对他来说，他只是看到了另一种人生，”塞万提斯说。
最终，路易斯自己做出了决定。当弟弟在加利福尼亚的一座山顶上获得“鹰、地球与锚”徽章时，塞万提斯就在现场。站在大约250名新晋海军陆战队员中间，塞万提斯几乎认不出自己正在寻找的那个人。
我简直不敢相信那就是他，”他说。“我看着的是我的弟弟，但那是个成年男人。我觉得我这辈子从没被任何人抱得那么紧。
当他们走下山时，路易斯本可以留在兄弟身边享受这一刻。但他却停下来帮助另一名正与背包较劲的新晋海军陆战队员。对塞万提斯来说，这才是衡量弟弟真正转变的标准。
我大概是感到最有成就感的人，”他说。“看到我弟弟说，‘我不会自私地留在这里跟你说话，’尽管他本来可以这么做。
在髋关节置换手术之后，塞万提斯找到了另一个指导年轻人的地方。受伤前，足球是他生活的重要组成部分。手术让他能够再次踢球。他开始当教练，后来又转做裁判。
球场上没有任何问题，”他说。“90分钟里，其他一切都不重要。无论我有什么痛苦、抑郁或焦虑，都会消失。
Cervantes为青少年、高中、大学和学院级别足球赛担任裁判，这给了他另一个机会去鼓励那些正在学习如何竞争、克服挫折和成长的年轻人。
你能看到这些孩子长大，你能看到这些孩子进步并做出更好的决定，”他说。“你能指导他们、和他们交谈并鞭策他们。
他把裁判工作视为未来可能从事的职业，甚至梦想成为一名拥有紫心勋章的职业裁判，这是他以前从未见过的殊荣。
在服役18年后，Cervantes知道他们这一代人最终必须将掌控权移交给下一代。他相信今天的年轻人能够获取信息、技术和资源，这些可以帮助他们变得更强、更有能力。他说，他的责任是确保他们拥有利用这些优势的工具。这包括教给他们一些他认为比任何技术技能都更重要的东西。
你不必为了在生活中取得成功而改变自己，”他说。“你只需要做一个好人。有时候，叫出某人的名字，给他们一句真诚的赞美——你就能改变他们的生活，因为你永远不知道人们正在经历什么。
无论是指导一位新任高级领导者、鼓励一名申请者、看着自己的弟弟成为海军陆战队员，还是手握哨子站在中场，塞万提斯都继续帮助他人前行，并鼓励他们绝不让挫折决定下一步。

items.title: Chaplain of the Marine Corps visits Camp Lejeune
items.author: LCpl Ethan Claassen
items.summary: MARINE CORPS BASE CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. — Rear Adm. Robert Christian, chaplain of the Marine Corps, Deputy Chief of Chaplains of the Navy and Deputy Director of Religious Ministries, visits Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune on Oct. 7, 2026.
items.body:
MARINE CORPS BASE CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. — Rear Adm. Robert Christian, chaplain of the Marine Corps, Deputy Chief of Chaplains of the Navy and Deputy Director of Religious Ministries, visits Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune on Oct. 7, 2026.

Christian assumed the duties as the 22nd Chaplain of the Marine Corps in July of this year. The Chaplain of the Marine Corps oversees religious ministry across the Corps, supporting spiritual readiness and advising leadership on religious, moral and ethical matters.

During his first visit with II Marine Expeditionary Force Religious Ministry Teams as the Chaplain of the Marine Corps, Christian reviewed Chaplain Corps initiatives such as overall readiness and what the Marine of 2040 will look like. Christian said, “The Marine of 2040 needs to be a Marine of character who can easily articulate what gives them inner strength for higher purpose.”

Christian noted that a leader’s role in a Marine’s spiritual fitness is just as important as a chaplain’s role among II MEF RMTs. Christian’s vision for the Chaplain Corps program does not rely on one chaplain, but on leaders who are built to carry the mission forward. “What we are trying to do is form a common language when it comes to what doing spiritual fitness looks like,” said Christian. “If we can start to talk about it that way, it’s going to empower the Marines and sailors under our lead to be able to run with themselves.”

Cmdr. Jonathan Stephens, deputy force chaplain with U.S. Marine Forces Command Religious Ministry Team, also spoke during the spiritual fitness brief emphasizing the transition from talking about spiritual fitness to practicing it. “We have developed a common language when it comes to spiritual fitness,” said Stephens. “Now we have to move from talk to walk.” Once the common language has been set in place for leaders to base their own spiritual fitness programs on, those programs must then be actioned.

Stephens identified three major challenges to spiritual fitness: the belief that it isn't for everyone, the risk of it becoming another "box to check" and the potential for alienation when practicing alone rather than in a group.

Stephens believes some Marines view spiritual fitness as inapplicable to them. “We have this opt out mentality,” said Stephens, emphasizing the importance of overcoming this ideology.

The second challenge is Marines receiving briefings but failing to act on the information. “If that’s where it stops, it’s as effective as sitting down, finding out a good workout routine and a good diet sitting in the classroom,” said Stephens. “It doesn’t work that way. There has to be some action that you take with that information.”

The third challenge involves the Marine Corps collective approach to operations. Stephens says if Marines practice spiritual fitness privately, it suggests the concept falls outside Marine Corps culture. “If we treat spiritual fitness like this individual home,” said Stephens, “It sends the message, if we don’t do it together, then this is not really in line with our Marine Corps.”

Using common language for leaders to build their own spiritual fitness programs helps overcome the challenges chaplains and leaders face when trying to implement spiritual fitness into operational readiness. Making a common language for these programs is the first step. To be effective, these programs must be put into action.

The purpose of Christian’s visit with II MEF RMTs was to discuss the future of Marine Corps spiritual fitness and emphasize its importance. Christian wants chaplains and leaders collaborating to encourage Marines to discuss their spiritual fitness. “I would really encourage you, as a chaplain, just be vocal about what gives you a reason to live,” said Christian. “Because people need to hear it, so it becomes an open conversation that we’re happy about.”
items.titleZh: 海军陆战队牧师长访问勒琼营海军陆战队基地
items.summaryZh: 北卡罗来纳州勒琼营海军陆战队基地——海军少将罗伯特·克里斯蒂安，海军陆战队牧师长、海军副牧师长兼宗教事务副主任，于2026年10月7日访问勒琼营海军陆战队基地。
zhParas: 北卡罗来纳州勒琼营海军陆战队基地——海军少将罗伯特·克里斯蒂安，海军陆战队牧师长、海军副牧师长兼宗教事务副主任，于2026年10月7日访问勒琼营海军陆战队基地。
克里斯蒂安于今年7月就任第22任海军陆战队牧师长。海军陆战队牧师长负责监督整个海军陆战队的宗教事务，支持精神战备，并就宗教、道德和伦理事务向领导层提供建议。
作为海军陆战队牧师长，克里斯蒂安在首次访问第二海军陆战队远征军宗教事务团队期间，审视了随军牧师团的各项举措，例如整体战备以及2040年的海军陆战队员将是什么样子。克里斯蒂安说：“2040年的海军陆战队员必须是有品格的海军陆战队员，能够轻松阐明是什么赋予他们为更高目标奋斗的内在力量。
克里斯蒂安指出，在海军陆战队员的精神强健方面，领导者的作用与牧师在第二海军陆战队远征军宗教事务团队中的作用同样重要。克里斯蒂安对随军牧师团项目的愿景并不依赖于某一位牧师，而是依赖于被培养为能够将这一使命向前推进的领导者。克里斯蒂安说：“我们试图做的是，就践行精神强健是什么样子形成一种共同语言。如果我们能开始以这种方式谈论它，就会赋能我们领导下的海军陆战队员和水兵，让他们能够自主推进。
美国海军陆战队部队司令部宗教事务团队副部队牧师、海军中校乔纳森·斯蒂芬斯也在精神强健简报上发言，强调要从谈论精神强健转向践行精神强健。斯蒂芬斯说：“在精神强健方面，我们已经形成了一种共同语言。现在我们必须从言谈转向行动。”一旦这种共同语言已经确立，使领导者能够以此为基础制定各自的精神强健计划，那么这些计划就必须付诸行动。
斯蒂芬斯指出精神强健面临的三大挑战：认为它并非适合所有人；它有可能变成又一个“打勾项”；以及独自而非在群体中践行时可能产生的疏离感。
斯蒂芬斯认为，一些海军陆战队员认为精神健康与他们无关。“我们存在这种选择退出的心态，”斯蒂芬斯说，并强调克服这种观念的重要性。
第二个挑战是海军陆战队员听取了简报，却没有根据这些信息采取行动。“如果事情到此为止，那就和坐在教室里了解一套好的锻炼方案和一份好的饮食计划一样有效，”斯蒂芬斯说。“这样做行不通。你必须根据这些信息采取一些行动。
第三个挑战涉及海军陆战队开展行动的集体方式。斯蒂芬斯说，如果海军陆战队员私下进行精神健康锻炼，就表明这一概念不属于海军陆战队文化。“如果我们把精神健康当作个人的家事，”斯蒂芬斯说，“这就传递出一个信息：如果我们不一起做，那它就不是真正符合我们海军陆战队的作风。
让领导者使用共同语言来制定自己的精神健康计划，有助于克服随军牧师和领导者在试图将精神健康纳入战备时面临的挑战。为这些计划制定共同语言是第一步。要行之有效，这些计划必须付诸行动。
克里斯蒂安访问第二海军陆战队远征军（II MEF）宗教事务团队（RMT）的目的，是讨论海军陆战队精神健康的未来并强调其重要性。克里斯蒂安希望随军牧师和领导者协作，鼓励海军陆战队员讨论他们的精神健康。“作为随军牧师，我真的鼓励你们大胆说出是什么给了你们活下去的理由，”克里斯蒂安说。“因为人们需要听到这些，这样它就会成为一场我们乐见的公开对话。

items.title: US Army activates new multi-domain task force to ‘deny, disrupt’ enemies in Indo-Pacific
items.author: Nikki Wentling
items.summary: The new 4th Multi-Domain Task Force includes four battalions and is planned to grow to 2,100 soldiers.
items.body:
A new U.S. Army multi-domain task force, one of five recently established or under development by the service, was activated this week with a ceremony at Fort Carson, Colorado.

The 4th Multi-Domain Task Force will focus on synchronizing long-range precision fires in the Indo-Pacific region “to deny, disrupt and disaggregate adversary capabilities” and create advantages for other units in the joint force, the Army said in a release.

The task force includes four battalions and is planned to grow to 2,100 soldiers.

Col. Hugh W.A. Jones assumed command of the task force during Thursday’s ceremony. He previously commanded the 2nd Stryker Brigade, 4th Infantry Division at Fort Carson, leading the brigade when it deployed to the U.S.-Mexico border last year.

“While we build this formation to deter aggression and preserve peace, if war comes, we must be prepared to fight and win,” Jones said during the ceremony. “We owe those in harm’s way every advantage we can give them, while leaving our enemy nowhere to run and nowhere to hide.”

The task force reports to the 7th Infantry Division at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington.

In June, the Army combined the 7th Infantry Division and the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force at Lewis-McChord into the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command-Pacific), which serves as the multi-domain operational headquarters. Its mission is to integrate “maneuver, fires, air defense, cyber, space, electronic warfare, intelligence, unmanned systems, sustainment and command-and -control in support of the joint force across the Pacific,” the Army said in a release.

Maj. Gen. Bernard Harrington, commander of the 7th Infantry Division, attended the activation ceremony at Fort Carson.

“You are driving the change our nation demands today, to meet the changing character of war, to prevent conflict, and to maintain a free and open Pacific alongside our allies and partners,” Harrington told soldiers assigned to the new multi-domain task force.

The establishment of the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command-Pacific) and the 4th Multi-Domain Task Force are part of a broader transformation initiative “to counter near-peer adversaries in an increasingly complex global landscape,” the Army said.

The initiative includes the service establishing five multi-domain task forces by 2028, according to a Congressional Research Service report. The Army activated the 2nd Multi-Domain Task Force in 2021 at the Clay Kaserne installation in Germany, and stood up the third in Hawaii in 2022. A fifth is planned for Fort Bragg, North Carolina.

The units are designed to operate across all domains — land, air, sea, space, cyberspace and information — and “provide combatant commanders with a versatile and potent array of options,” according to the Army.

“As we build this formation, we must never forget that technology earns its value in the hands of well-trained and disciplined soldiers,” Jones said Thursday. “A soldier who solves a difficult problem here may make the difference for an American fighting far beyond the horizon.”

Nikki Wentling is a senior editor at Military Times. She's reported on veterans and military communities for over a decade and has also covered technology, politics, health care and crime. Her work has earned multiple honors from the National Coalition for Homeless Veterans, the Arkansas Associated Press Managing Editors and others.
items.titleZh: 美国陆军启用新的多域特遣部队，以在印太地区“拒止、扰乱”敌人
items.summaryZh: 新的第4多域特遣部队下辖四个营，计划扩编至2100名士兵。
zhParas: 美国陆军一支新的多域特遣部队本周在科罗拉多州卡森堡举行仪式正式启用；这是该军种近期已成立或正在组建的五支此类部队之一。
美国陆军在一份新闻稿中表示，第4多域特遣部队将专注于在印太地区同步远程精确火力，“以拒止、扰乱和拆解对手能力”，并为联合部队其他单位创造优势。
该特遣部队下辖四个营，计划扩编至2100名士兵。
休·W·A·琼斯上校在周四的仪式上就任该特遣部队指挥官。他此前在卡森堡指挥美国陆军第4步兵师第2斯特赖克旅，并在该旅去年部署至美墨边境时担任指挥官。
琼斯在仪式上说：“我们组建这支部队，是为了威慑侵略、维护和平；但如果战争来临，我们必须准备好作战并取胜。我们应当为那些身处险境的人提供我们能给予的一切优势，同时让敌人无处可逃、无处可藏。
该特遣部队隶属于华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的第7步兵师。
6月，美国陆军将刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的第7步兵师和第1多域特遣队合并为第7步兵师（多域指挥-太平洋），作为多域作战司令部。美国陆军在一份新闻稿中表示，其任务是整合“机动、火力、防空、网络、太空、电子战、情报、无人系统、保障和指挥控制，以支持整个太平洋地区的联合部队”。
第7步兵师师长伯纳德·哈林顿少将出席了在卡森堡举行的成立仪式。
你们正在推动我们国家今天所要求的变革，以应对不断变化的战争特征，防止冲突，并与我们的盟友和伙伴一道维护自由开放的太平洋，”哈林顿对新组建多域特遣队的士兵们说。
美国陆军表示，成立第7步兵师（多域指挥-太平洋）和第4多域特遣队，是更广泛转型计划的一部分，旨在“在日益复杂的全球格局中对抗近乎同级的对手”。
根据美国国会研究服务处的一份报告，该计划包括美国陆军在2028年前建立五支多域特遣队。美国陆军于2021年在德国克莱军营成立第2多域特遣队，并于2022年在夏威夷成立第三支。第五支计划设在北卡罗来纳州布拉格堡。
据美国陆军称，这些部队旨在跨所有领域——陆、空、海、太空、网络空间和信息——作战，并“为作战指挥官提供多样化且强大的选项”。
在我们打造这支部队时，我们绝不能忘记，技术的价值是在训练有素、纪律严明的士兵手中实现的，”琼斯周四说。“一名在这里解决难题的士兵，可能会为一名远在地平线之外作战的美国人带来关键改变。
妮基·温特林是《军事时报》的高级编辑。她报道退伍军人和军事社区已有十多年，也曾报道技术、政治、医疗保健和犯罪。她的作品获得了全国无家可归退伍军人联盟、阿肯色州美联社编辑管理者协会等机构颁发的多项荣誉。

第7步兵师师长伯纳德·哈林顿少将出席了在卡森堡举行的成立仪式。

你们正在推动我们国家今天所要求的变革，以应对不断变化的战争特征，防止冲突，并与我们的盟友和伙伴一道维护自由开放的太平洋，”哈林顿对新组建多域特遣队的士兵们说。

美国陆军表示，成立第7步兵师（多域指挥-太平洋）和第4多域特遣队，是更广泛转型计划的一部分，旨在“在日益复杂的全球格局中对抗近乎同级的对手”。

根据美国国会研究服务处的一份报告，该计划包括美国陆军在2028年前建立五支多域特遣队。美国陆军于2021年在德国克莱军营成立第2多域特遣队，并于2022年在夏威夷成立第三支。第五支计划设在北卡罗来纳州布拉格堡。

据美国陆军称，这些部队旨在跨所有领域——陆、空、海、太空、网络空间和信息——作战，并“为作战指挥官提供多样化且强大的选项”。

在我们打造这支部队时，我们绝不能忘记，技术的价值是在训练有素、纪律严明的士兵手中实现的，”琼斯周四说。“一名在这里解决难题的士兵，可能会为一名远在地平线之外作战的美国人带来关键改变。

妮基·温特林是《军事时报》的高级编辑。她报道退伍军人和军事社区已有十多年，也曾报道技术、政治、医疗保健和犯罪。她的作品获得了全国无家可归退伍军人联盟、阿肯色州美联社编辑管理者协会等机构颁发的多项荣誉。

items.body:
Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii— In the summer of 2025, in a corner of a machine shop at Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY & IMF), Able Seaman Colby Morley disassembled a pressure valve for testing. It’s the kind of hands-on job he’d rarely get to do back home as an avionics technician with the Royal Australian Navy.

As part of a first-of-its-kind training rotation, Morley was one of 20 Royal Australian Navy Fleet Support Unit (FSU) sailors who trained in Hawaii to learn how to maintain U.S. nuclear-powered attack submarines. The cross-functional team was stationed in Pearl Harbor from June through October of last year and completed an intensive U.S.-led training rotation before returning home to support USS Vermont’s (SSN 792) submarine maintenance period at HMAS Stirling in Western Australia in November 2025.

“The team is a small but very important cog in the wheel for AUKUS. Our main goal is making sure Australia is self-reliable when it comes to the maintenance of these newer assets,” said Royal Australian Navy Chief Petty Officer Steven Sheakey, the deployed maintenance team’s senior technical officer. “The fleet support units are going to play an important role in delivering maintenance to the U.S. assets that are going to be rotating through HMAS Stirling. So, the knowledge, experiences and cohesive relationships we’ve got with U.S. personnel—both civilian and in uniform—are going to play a vital role moving forward to ensure we’re interoperable in the future.”

In the U.S., the FSU team’s mission was to gain maintenance experience on U.S. platforms, build technical interoperability and prepare to sustain U.S. and U.K. nuclear-powered submarines. Under the AUKUS agreement, the U.S. and U.K. are supporting Australia’s efforts to acquire, maintain and sustain its own sovereign fleet of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines—a departure from Australia’s current fleet of diesel-electric submarines.

Submarine Rotational Force-West, or SRF-West, is one of the AUKUS partnership’s key outcomes. The initiative will see U.S. Virginia-class and U.K. Astute-class submarines rotate out of the Royal Australian Navy’s submarine base in the Indian Ocean, HMAS Stirling*,* for an extended period, starting in 2027.

Strategic Sustainment Starts with People

The team sent to Hawaii was drawn from across the Royal Australian Navy’s five FSUs and selected through a competitive, skills-based screening process. The sailors’ specialties range from electronics to propulsion to weapons, reflecting the future workforce Australia will need to support Australian-flagged nuclear-powered submarines.

“We needed a team that could embed anywhere, adapt quickly and represent the full scope of Navy engineering,” said Royal Australian Navy Lt. Zachery Telfser, officer in charge of the deployed maintenance team. “This isn’t just submarine work—it’s about building a broad, interoperable sustainment workforce that can flex with future mission demands.”

Some sailors, like Morely, are outside the traditional submarine pipeline. But as Australia expands its readiness to support nuclear propulsion, the Royal Australian Navy is pulling from across its engineering enterprise to identify who can contribute to the overall mission.

“We’re stress-testing the system,” Sheakey said. “In Australia, we multi-train our sailors so they can wear more than one hat. That kind of flexibility is essential to building interoperable teams who can deliver complex submarine maintenance packages at SRF-West.”

Fleet Support Unit-West sailors will serve as SRF-West's primary uniformed maintenance workforce. More than 200 personnel from the Australian Submarine Agency’s civilian sustainment partner, ASC Pty. Ltd., are also training in Hawaii to lead intermediate- and depot-level maintenance work on Australia’s future fleet of fast-attack submarines. Both the Fleet Support Unit and ASC teams put their newfound skills to the test during the November 2025 submarine maintenance period at HMAS Stirling in Western Australia.

“This joint workforce approach combining the U.S. Navy, Royal Australian Navy and Australian civilians is central to how SRF-West will operate,” said Elizabeth Tolin, the deputy division head for SRF-West at the U.S. Navy’s AUKUS Integration and Acquisition program office. “Our work with Australia is enabling us to build a cohesive, interoperable sustainment enterprise.”

These joint efforts align directly with the Department of War’s May 2026 announcement formally establishing Naval Support Activity Stirling and reestablishing Submarine Squadron 3. PHNSY &IMF, which was previously named the lead maintenance activity for SRF-West, is actively preparing to deploy its maintenance detachment to Western Australia where American personnel will continue working alongside their FSU and ASC maintenance counterparts.

Learning to Work Together, Technically and Culturally

For Royal Australian Navy Leading Seaman Jayden Webb, an electronics technician, the rotation was his second stint working with the U.S. Navy, and another opportunity to refine shared maintenance insights.

“We’re doing more than just fixing systems,” he said in an interview alongside Morely last August. “We’re learning how the U.S. Navy thinks about readiness, risk and reporting. That’s what it’ll take to maintain and sustain these platforms safely and confidently back in Australia.”

Webb embedded with the U.S. Navy’s Performance Monitoring Team, which performs rigorous testing and diagnostics aboard submarines. Others, like Morely, worked in the shipyard’s machine shop, rebuilding and testing valves under the mentorship of experienced U.S. tradesmen.

“At home, we’re used to getting a tech order that tells us what’s wrong,” Morely said. “At Pearl, we’re learning how to troubleshoot from scratch. It’s taught me to be more comfortable with uncertainty and more deliberate about communication.”

From Pearl Harbor to Perth

In October 2025, the team returned to Western Australia to complete their mission by performing maintenance aboard USS Vermont during its planned submarine maintenance period*.*

The submarine maintenance period, which lasted through November, marked a historic milestone underscoring the momentum of AUKUS and its vision for enhanced deterrence and industrial resilience in the Indo-Pacific. For Australia, it’s also an opportunity to evaluate its long-term investment in submarine sustainment and sovereign capability.

“The submarine maintenance period was a big step forward from when we had a U.S. submarine tender, USS Emory S. Land (AS 39) across the pier from USS Hawaii (SSN 776) in August 2024 to oversee and execute the submarine tendered maintenance period,” said Rear Adm. Doug Adams, director, AUKUS, International & Systems. “For Vermont, we had a larger work package, a truly blended maintenance workforce led by Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Activity, and when that boat left to operate in the Indo-Pacific region, it was ready for any tasking.”

As Australia continues to build capacity to own, operate and maintain nuclear-powered submarines, sailors from the FSU will continue to support U.S. submarine maintenance periods, including the next one scheduled to occur in Western Australia by the end of 2026.

“We’ve still got a lot of work ahead,” said Sheakey. “Australia’s got to grow its infrastructure, procedures and people. But, we’re proving we’re up to the task, and that we’re a capable, committed partner.”

For sailors like Morely and Webb, the experience has also reshaped how they think about their roles in a trilateral security framework.

“To me, AUKUS is about bringing our forces together, not just in strategy, but in day-to-day operations,” said Webb. “It’s exciting to be part of something this big.”

“This was my first time outside Australia,” Morely added. “To be in Hawaii, working with the U.S. Navy on something that’s going to have such a big impact back home—that means a lot.”
items.titleZh: 锻造前线盟友：澳大利亚皇家海军维修人员学习美国潜艇保障以增强太平洋战备
items.summaryZh: 2025年夏天，在珍珠港海军造船厂暨中级维护设施（PHNSY & IMF）一个机加工车间的角落里，一等水兵科尔比·莫利拆开了一个压力阀以进行测试。作为澳大利亚皇家海军的航空电子技术员，他在国内很少有机会做这种动手操作的工作。作为首次此类训练轮换的一部分，莫利是20名在夏威夷接受培训的澳大利亚皇家海军舰队支援部队（FSU）水兵之一，他们学习如何维护美国……
zhParas: 夏威夷珍珠港-希卡姆联合基地——2025年夏天，在珍珠港海军造船厂暨中级维护设施（PHNSY & IMF）一个机加工车间的角落里，一等水兵科尔比·莫利拆开了一个压力阀以进行测试。作为澳大利亚皇家海军的航空电子技术员，他在国内很少有机会做这种动手操作的工作。
作为一次首开先例的训练轮换的一部分，莫利是20名澳大利亚皇家海军舰队支援部队（FSU）水兵之一，他们在夏威夷接受训练，学习如何维护美国核动力攻击潜艇。这个跨职能团队去年6月至10月驻扎在珍珠港，完成了美方主导的密集训练轮换，随后于2025年11月返回国内，支援位于澳大利亚西部的斯特灵海军基地内美国“佛蒙特”号（SSN 792）潜艇的维护期。
这个团队是奥库斯联盟车轮上一个虽小但非常重要的齿轮。我们的主要目标是确保澳大利亚在这些较新装备的维护方面能够自力更生，”澳大利亚皇家海军军士长史蒂文·希基说，他是部署维护团队的高级技术官。“舰队支援部队将在为轮换驻留斯特灵海军基地的美方装备提供维护方面发挥重要作用。因此，我们与美国人员——无论是文职人员还是军人——所获得的知识、经验和紧密关系，将在未来发挥至关重要的作用，确保我们未来能够互操作。
在美国，FSU团队的任务是获取美方平台维护经验、建立技术互操作性，并为维持美国和英国核动力潜艇做好准备。根据奥库斯联盟协议，美国和英国正在支持澳大利亚获取、维护和维持其自身主权所有的常规武装核动力潜艇舰队——这与澳大利亚现有的柴电潜艇舰队不同。
潜艇轮换部队-西部”（SRF-West）是奥库斯联盟伙伴关系的关键成果之一。该倡议将使美国“弗吉尼亚”级和英国“机敏”级潜艇从2027年开始，长期轮换部署于澳大利亚皇家海军位于印度洋的潜艇基地——斯特灵海军基地。
战略保障始于人
派往夏威夷的团队从澳大利亚皇家海军五支舰队保障部队（FSU）中抽调，并经过竞争性的、基于技能的筛选流程选拔。这些水兵的专业范围从电子到推进再到武器，反映出澳大利亚未来支持悬挂澳大利亚国旗的核动力潜艇所需的劳动力。
我们需要一支能够嵌入任何地方、快速适应并代表海军工程全貌的团队，”澳大利亚皇家海军上尉扎卡里·特尔夫瑟（Zachery Telfser）说，他是部署维修团队的负责人。“这不仅仅是潜艇工作——而是要建立一支广泛、可互操作的保障队伍，能够根据未来任务需求灵活调整。
一些水兵，例如莫利，并不属于传统的潜艇培养路径。但随着澳大利亚扩大其支持核推进的战备能力，澳大利亚皇家海军正从其整个工程体系中抽调人员，以确定谁能为总体任务作出贡献。
我们正在对系统进行压力测试，”希基说。“在澳大利亚，我们对水兵进行多岗位培训，使他们能够身兼数职。这种灵活性对于在SRF-West交付复杂潜艇维修包的可互操作团队至关重要。
舰队保障部队-西部的水兵将作为SRF-West的主要穿制服维修队伍。来自澳大利亚潜艇局民用保障合作伙伴ASC Pty. Ltd.的200多名人员也在夏威夷接受培训，以领导澳大利亚未来快速攻击潜艇舰队的中继级和基地级维修工作。舰队保障部队和ASC团队都在2025年11月于西澳大利亚HMAS斯特灵进行的潜艇维修期间，对新掌握的技能进行了检验。
这种联合美国海军、澳大利亚皇家海军和澳大利亚文职人员的联合队伍模式，是SRF-West运作方式的核心，”美国海军奥库斯联盟一体化与采办项目办公室负责SRF-West的副部门主管伊丽莎白·托林说。“我们与澳大利亚的合作使我们能够建立一个有凝聚力、可互操作的保障体系。
这些联合努力直接契合美国战争部2026年5月的声明，该声明正式设立斯特灵海军支援设施，并重建第3潜艇中队。珍珠港海军造船厂与中间维护设施（PHNSY & IMF）此前被指定为SRF-West的牵头维修单位，目前正积极准备将其维修分遣队部署到西澳大利亚；在那里，美国人员将继续与FSU和ASC的维修同行并肩工作。
在技术与文化上学会协同工作
对澳大利亚皇家海军电子技术员、上等水兵杰登·韦布而言，这次轮换是他第二次与美国海军共事，也是又一次完善共同维修认知的机会。
我们做的不仅仅是修理系统，”去年8月他与莫利一同接受采访时说。“我们正在学习美国海军如何看待战备、风险和报告。回到澳大利亚后，要安全而自信地维护和保障这些平台，就需要这样做。
韦布被编入美国海军性能监测团队，该团队在潜艇上执行严格的测试与诊断。像莫利这样的其他人则在船厂机加工车间工作，在美国经验丰富的技工指导下重新组装并测试阀门。
在国内，我们习惯了拿到一份技术指令，告诉我们哪里出了问题，”莫利说。“在珍珠港，我们正在学习如何从头排查故障。这教会我更从容地面对不确定性，也更审慎地沟通。
从珍珠港到珀斯
2025年10月，该团队返回西澳大利亚，在计划中的潜艇维护期内登上美国海军‘佛蒙特’号（USS Vermont）执行维护，以此完成任务。
这一潜艇维护期持续到11月，标志着一个历史性里程碑，凸显了奥库斯联盟的发展势头及其在印太地区增强威慑和工业韧性的愿景。对澳大利亚而言，这也是评估其在潜艇保障和主权能力方面长期投资的机会。

这一潜艇维护期相比2024年8月向前迈出了一大步；当时我们有一艘美国潜艇供应舰‘埃默里·S·兰德’号（AS 39）停靠在码头，‘夏威夷’号（SSN 776）就在其对面，由它监督并执行潜艇供应舰维护期，”奥库斯联盟、国际与系统事务主任道格·亚当斯海军少将说。“就‘佛蒙特’号而言，我们的工作包更大，维护队伍真正实现了混合编组，由珍珠港海军造船厂与中级维修机构牵头；当该艇离开前往印太地区执行任务时，它已准备好承担任何任务。
随着澳大利亚继续建设拥有、运营和维护核动力潜艇的能力，来自舰队支援部队（FSU）的水兵将继续支持美国潜艇维护期，包括计划于2026年底前在西澳大利亚进行的下一次维护期。
我们前方仍有许多工作要做，”希基说。“澳大利亚必须发展其基础设施、程序流程和人员队伍。但我们正在证明自己能够胜任这项任务，也正在证明我们是一个有能力、坚定投入的伙伴。
对于像莫利和韦布这样的水兵来说，这段经历也重塑了他们对自身在三边安全框架中所扮演角色的看法。
在我看来，奥库斯联盟的意义在于把我们的部队凝聚在一起，不仅体现在战略上，更体现在日常行动中，”韦布说。“能参与如此重大的事情，令人兴奋。
这是我第一次走出澳大利亚，”莫利补充道。“来到夏威夷，与美国海军合作开展一项将对国内产生如此重大影响的事情——这对我意义重大。

我们需要一支能够嵌入任何地方、快速适应并代表海军工程全貌的团队，”澳大利亚皇家海军上尉扎卡里·特尔夫瑟（Zachery Telfser）说，他是部署维修团队的负责人。“这不仅仅是潜艇工作——而是要建立一支广泛、可互操作的保障队伍，能够根据未来任务需求灵活调整。

一些水兵，例如莫利，并不属于传统的潜艇培养路径。但随着澳大利亚扩大其支持核推进的战备能力，澳大利亚皇家海军正从其整个工程体系中抽调人员，以确定谁能为总体任务作出贡献。

我们正在对系统进行压力测试，”希基说。“在澳大利亚，我们对水兵进行多岗位培训，使他们能够身兼数职。这种灵活性对于在SRF-West交付复杂潜艇维修包的可互操作团队至关重要。

舰队保障部队-西部的水兵将作为SRF-West的主要穿制服维修队伍。来自澳大利亚潜艇局民用保障合作伙伴ASC Pty. Ltd.的200多名人员也在夏威夷接受培训，以领导澳大利亚未来快速攻击潜艇舰队的中继级和基地级维修工作。舰队保障部队和ASC团队都在2025年11月于西澳大利亚HMAS斯特灵进行的潜艇维修期间，对新掌握的技能进行了检验。

这种联合美国海军、澳大利亚皇家海军和澳大利亚文职人员的联合队伍模式，是SRF-West运作方式的核心，”美国海军奥库斯联盟一体化与采办项目办公室负责SRF-West的副部门主管伊丽莎白·托林说。“我们与澳大利亚的合作使我们能够建立一个有凝聚力、可互操作的保障体系。

这些联合努力直接契合美国战争部2026年5月的声明，该声明正式设立斯特灵海军支援设施，并重建第3潜艇中队。珍珠港海军造船厂与中间维护设施（PHNSY & IMF）此前被指定为SRF-West的牵头维修单位，目前正积极准备将其维修分遣队部署到西澳大利亚；在那里，美国人员将继续与FSU和ASC的维修同行并肩工作。

在技术与文化上学会协同工作

对澳大利亚皇家海军电子技术员、上等水兵杰登·韦布而言，这次轮换是他第二次与美国海军共事，也是又一次完善共同维修认知的机会。

我们做的不仅仅是修理系统，”去年8月他与莫利一同接受采访时说。“我们正在学习美国海军如何看待战备、风险和报告。回到澳大利亚后，要安全而自信地维护和保障这些平台，就需要这样做。

韦布被编入美国海军性能监测团队，该团队在潜艇上执行严格的测试与诊断。像莫利这样的其他人则在船厂机加工车间工作，在美国经验丰富的技工指导下重新组装并测试阀门。

在国内，我们习惯了拿到一份技术指令，告诉我们哪里出了问题，”莫利说。“在珍珠港，我们正在学习如何从头排查故障。这教会我更从容地面对不确定性，也更审慎地沟通。

从珍珠港到珀斯

2025年10月，该团队返回西澳大利亚，在计划中的潜艇维护期内登上美国海军‘佛蒙特’号（USS Vermont）执行维护，以此完成任务。

这一潜艇维护期持续到11月，标志着一个历史性里程碑，凸显了奥库斯联盟的发展势头及其在印太地区增强威慑和工业韧性的愿景。对澳大利亚而言，这也是评估其在潜艇保障和主权能力方面长期投资的机会。

这一潜艇维护期相比2024年8月向前迈出了一大步；当时我们有一艘美国潜艇供应舰‘埃默里·S·兰德’号（AS 39）停靠在码头，‘夏威夷’号（SSN 776）就在其对面，由它监督并执行潜艇供应舰维护期，”奥库斯联盟、国际与系统事务主任道格·亚当斯海军少将说。“就‘佛蒙特’号而言，我们的工作包更大，维护队伍真正实现了混合编组，由珍珠港海军造船厂与中级维修机构牵头；当该艇离开前往印太地区执行任务时，它已准备好承担任何任务。

随着澳大利亚继续建设拥有、运营和维护核动力潜艇的能力，来自舰队支援部队（FSU）的水兵将继续支持美国潜艇维护期，包括计划于2026年底前在西澳大利亚进行的下一次维护期。

我们前方仍有许多工作要做，”希基说。“澳大利亚必须发展其基础设施、程序流程和人员队伍。但我们正在证明自己能够胜任这项任务，也正在证明我们是一个有能力、坚定投入的伙伴。

对于像莫利和韦布这样的水兵来说，这段经历也重塑了他们对自身在三边安全框架中所扮演角色的看法。

在我看来，奥库斯联盟的意义在于把我们的部队凝聚在一起，不仅体现在战略上，更体现在日常行动中，”韦布说。“能参与如此重大的事情，令人兴奋。

这是我第一次走出澳大利亚，”莫利补充道。“来到夏威夷，与美国海军合作开展一项将对国内产生如此重大影响的事情——这对我意义重大。

items.title: Watchdog Urges Better Alignment Across Pentagon’s Planned GPS Backups
items.author: Courtney Albon
items.summary: All of the U.S. military services are pursuing capabilities to complement GPS amid concerns that the constellation is increasingly vulnerable to interference, but a new government watchdog report calls for better coordination and prioritization among those efforts to avoid delays and duplication. The post Watchdog Urges Better Alignment Across Pentagon’s Planned GPS Backups appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
All of the U.S. military services are pursuing capabilities to complement GPS amid concerns that the constellation is increasingly vulnerable to interference, but a new government watchdog report calls for better coordination and prioritization among those efforts to avoid delays and duplication.

Today’s GPS constellation is a mix of new and legacy satellites, the oldest of which are nearly 30 years old. The system has become essential to the entire global economy, affecting industries like agriculture, banking, and transportation, which are dependent on the system for timing and positioning. It’s also a fundamental military capability, particularly important for navigating in remote areas and helping guide missiles and drones.

In recent years, U.S. leaders have sounded the alarm about GPS vulnerabilities, especially jamming and spoofing. Because the Pentagon is dependent on space for precision targeting and communications, signal disruption poses a growing threat. Efforts to modernize GPS satellite, ground, and user equipment have faced repeated delays, exacerbating those concerns.

The Air Force, Space Force, Army, Navy, and Marine Corps have all pursued programs to either augment GPS capabilities or serve as a backup should the constellation be unavailable. For example, the Space Development Agency and the Army are fielding positioning, navigation, and timing, or PNT, satellites in low-Earth orbit, and the Navy is developing a PNT receiver that can calculate a ship’s position without the use of GPS using celestial bodies like stars, planets, and satellites on predictable orbits.

While these efforts have seen various degrees of success, an Oct. 7 report from the Government Accountability Office highlights risks within the current GPS modernization plans and the services’ various alternative PNT pursuits.

“Ineffective coordination of the fragmented interdependent PNT efforts among multiple military services—sometimes across more than one—hampers efficient alignment of those efforts,” GAO says in its report. “Pursuing modernized GPS and complementary PNT technologies to augment GPS requires foresight and planning. Integration timelines for weapon systems are often lengthy, and schedules must be properly aligned for the development of such modernized PNT technologies and their integration into weapon systems.”

As an example, GAO points to efforts to upgrade munitions to use M-code, a specialized, secure GPS signal. If the munitions have an integrated M-code capability before the aircraft, ships and ground platforms that fire them—which GAO says is likely to occur—that could cause synchronization issues before and after launch since positions are usually passed from a platform to a munition.

The report notes that officials has made some steps to consolidate PNT development efforts into joint program offices but argues more is needed. The agency recommends the Army, Navy, and Department of the Air Force identify opportunities to consolidate complementary programs to “ensure better strategic alignment with DOD and the other services” and drive efficiency.

“These efficiencies may improve schedule alignments between interdependent programs and ease the realignment of resources for higher priority programs within the portfolio to ensure that warfighters obtain these necessary capabilities to address current and future threats,” GAO writes.
items.titleZh: 监督机构敦促五角大楼计划中的GPS备份系统加强协调
items.summaryZh: 美国所有军种都在寻求补充GPS的能力，原因是人们担心GPS卫星星座越来越容易受到干扰，但一份新的政府监督机构报告呼吁在这些努力之间加强协调和优先排序，以避免延误和重复。监督机构敦促五角大楼计划中的GPS备份系统加强协调。该文章首发于《空军与太空军杂志》。
zhParas: 美国所有军种都在寻求补充GPS的能力，原因是人们担心GPS卫星星座越来越容易受到干扰，但一份新的政府监督机构报告呼吁在这些努力之间加强协调和优先排序，以避免延误和重复。
当今的GPS卫星星座由新卫星和老旧卫星混合组成，其中最早的卫星已近30年。该系统已成为整个全球经济不可或缺的一部分，影响着农业、银行业和交通运输等行业，这些行业依赖该系统进行授时和定位。它也是一种基本军事能力，对于在偏远地区导航以及帮助引导导弹和无人机尤为重要。
近年来，美国领导人已就GPS的脆弱性发出警告，尤其是干扰和欺骗。由于五角大楼依赖太空进行精确瞄准和通信，信号中断构成了日益严重的威胁。对GPS卫星、地面设备和用户设备进行现代化的努力一再遭遇延误，加剧了这些担忧。
美国空军、太空军、陆军、海军和海军陆战队都推行了相关项目，以增强GPS能力，或在GPS星座不可用时作为备份。例如，太空发展局和陆军正在低地球轨道部署定位、导航与授时（PNT）卫星，而海军正在开发一种PNT接收机，该接收机无需使用GPS，而是利用恒星、行星和处于可预测轨道上的卫星等天体来计算舰艇位置。
尽管这些努力取得了不同程度的成功，但美国政府问责局10月7日的一份报告强调了当前GPS现代化计划以及各军种各种替代性PNT工作所面临的风险。
多个军种之间分散且相互依赖的PNT工作——有时还涉及不止一个军种——若协调不力，就会妨碍对这些工作的有效统筹，”政府问责局在其报告中表示。“推进现代化GPS和补充性PNT技术以增强GPS需要远见和规划。武器系统的集成时间表往往很长，必须妥善协调此类现代化PNT技术的开发及其集成到武器系统中的进度安排。
例如，美国政府问责局指出，为弹药升级以使用M码——一种专用、安全的GPS信号——所做的努力。如果弹药在发射它们的飞机、舰艇和地面平台之前就具备集成的M码能力——美国政府问责局称这种情况很可能发生——那么这可能在发射前后引发同步问题，因为位置通常由平台传递给弹药。
报告指出，官员们已采取一些措施，将定位、导航与授时（PNT）开发工作整合到联合项目办公室，但认为还需要做得更多。该机构建议陆军、海军和空军部找出整合互补项目的机会，以“确保与国防部及其他军种更好地实现战略对齐”，并提高效率。
美国政府问责局写道：“这些效率可能改善相互依赖项目之间的进度协调，并便于在项目组合内为更高优先级项目重新调配资源，以确保作战人员获得应对当前和未来威胁所需的这些能力。

items.title: New Procedure Lets Maintainers See ‘Blind Spot’ in F-16 Engine That Caused Crashes
items.author: Greg Hadley
items.summary: The Air Force has figured out a way for maintainers to inspect what had been a “blind spot” in F-16 engines, after problems in that area led to the catastrophic crashes of two jets in recent years. The post New Procedure Lets Maintainers See ‘Blind Spot’ in F-16 Engine That Caused Crashes appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
The Air Force has figured out a way for maintainers to inspect what had been a “blind spot” in F-16 engines, after problems in that area led to the catastrophic crashes of two jets in recent years.

A spokesperson for the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center confirmed the new procedure to Air & Space Forces Magazine last month. Task & Purpose first reported the development.

AFLCMC’s propulsion directorate developed the new process, which does not require any modifications to the engine or new equipment, the spokesperson added. The inspections is meant specifically for Pratt & Whitney F100 engine models—some F-16s are powered by GE Aerospace F110 models.

The F100 engine consists of 13 “stages,” each with variable vanes and compressor blades. Air flows through the stages, which rotate to accelerate, compress, and then regulate the airflow before releasing it into the engine’s combustion chamber. If a vane is turned or misaligned, however, it creates “abnormal aerodynamic forces” and “irregular wake patterns” that put stress on the compressor blades in the following stages, according to Air Force reports. That can lead to vanes or blades cracking or breaking, causing the entire engine to fail.

Maintainers can inspect many of the F100 engine’s stages using a borescope—a camera mounted on a flexible tube. There are even borescope ports for them to do so. But the fourth and especially the fifth stages are hard to reach. Before the development of this new inspection process, the Air Force said it was impossible for maintainers to inspect them without completely disassembling the engine, something only done at depots and not while the engine is installed on the aircraft.

This blind spot proved dangerous. An F-16 crashed near Holloman Air Force Base, N.M., in April 2024, and another jet, belonging to the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds, crashed in the California desert in December 2025. Subsequent investigations determined that in both cases, the F-16s’ engines had failed because of misaligned vanes in the fifth stage.

The pilots in both crashes were able to safely eject, but both jets were completely destroyed and the total damages exceeded $54 million.

Notably, both F-16 engines in question had experienced foreign object debris, or FOD, events in the years prior to the crashes. In both cases, maintainers noted damage to early stages of the inlet fan but found no issues with the fourth, seventh, or eighth stages—and the F-16’s technical orders did not require maintainers to remove and disassemble the engine core to inspect the fifth and sixth stages after a FOD event if no damage is found in the surrounding stages.

While investigators were unable to conclusively say if the FOD events led to the vanes becoming misaligned, the Air Force has now updated its technical orders to require the new inspection procedure to check the fifth stage of the engine after every FOD event.

“Additionally, the program office has worked with Pratt & Whitney to redesign the vane arm to be more impact resistant. The new design is qualified, on order, and will be installed via forced retrofit as soon as available,” the AFLCMC spokesperson said.
items.titleZh: 新程序让维护人员看到导致坠机的F-16发动机“盲区
items.summaryZh: 美国空军已找到一种方法，让维护人员能够检查F-16发动机中此前存在的“盲区”，因为近年来该区域的问题曾导致两架战机灾难性坠毁。《新程序让维护人员看到导致坠机的F-16发动机“盲区”》一文最初发表于《空军与太空军杂志》。
zhParas: 美国空军已找到一种方法，让维护人员能够检查F-16发动机中此前存在的“盲区”；近年来，该区域的问题曾导致两架战机灾难性坠毁。
美国空军生命周期管理中心的一位发言人上个月向《空天军杂志》证实了这一新程序。《任务与目的》最先报道了这一进展。
空军生命周期管理中心的推进局开发了这一新流程，该流程不需要对发动机进行任何改装，也不需要新设备，这位发言人补充说。该检查专门针对普惠F100发动机型号——部分F-16由GE航空航天公司的F110发动机提供动力。
F100发动机由13个“级”组成，每一级都有可调导叶和压气机叶片。空气流经这些级，这些级会旋转，以加速、压缩并调节气流，然后将气流释放到发动机燃烧室中。然而，根据美国空军报告，如果导叶发生转动或错位，就会产生“异常气动力”和“不规则尾流形态”，从而给后续级的压气机叶片施加应力。这可能导致导叶或叶片开裂或断裂，致使整个发动机失效。
维护人员可以使用孔探仪——一种安装在柔性管上的摄像头——检查F100发动机的许多级。发动机上甚至设有供他们这样做的孔探口。但第4级，尤其是第5级，很难接触到。美国空军表示，在开发这一新检查流程之前，维护人员若不将发动机完全拆解，就不可能检查这些级；而完全拆解只能在维修基地进行，且不能在发动机仍安装在飞机上时进行。
这个盲区被证明很危险。2024年4月，一架F-16在新墨西哥州霍洛曼空军基地附近坠毁；2025年12月，另一架属于美国空军“雷鸟”飞行表演队的战机在加利福尼亚州沙漠中坠毁。随后的调查确定，在这两起事故中，F-16的发动机都因第5级导叶错位而失效。
两起坠机事故中的飞行员均安全弹射逃生，但两架战机均完全损毁，总损失超过5400万美元。
值得注意的是，涉事的两台F-16发动机在坠机前数年都曾发生过外来物碎片（FOD）事件。在这两起案例中，维护人员都注意到进气道风扇前几级存在损伤，但未发现第四级、第七级或第八级有问题——而F-16的技术规程并未要求维护人员在FOD事件后、若相邻级未发现损伤时，拆卸并分解发动机核心机以检查第五级和第六级。
虽然调查人员无法最终确定FOD事件是否导致叶片错位，但美国空军现已更新其技术规程，要求每次FOD事件后都采用新的检查程序检查发动机第五级。
此外，项目办公室已与普惠公司合作，重新设计叶片臂，使其更抗冲击。新设计已通过认证，已下单，并将在可用后尽快通过强制改装进行安装，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）发言人说。

items.title: West Coast Vibe(s) Coding
items.author: BrianBrian Block
items.summary: The Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Mission Systems Overmatch Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) hosted an artificial intelligence vibe coding demonstration at Naval Base Point Loma’s Old Town campus for dozens of information technology professionals and senior leaders Sept. 16 and 17. The demonstration showed what is capable with agentic coding tools and the value that they can bring to the development, security, and operations pipeline.
items.body:
SAN DIEGO – The Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Mission Systems Overmatch Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) hosted an artificial intelligence vibe coding demonstration at Naval Base Point Loma’s Old Town campus for dozens of information technology professionals and senior leaders Sept. 16 and 17.

Vibe coding is when humans prompt an AI agent using regular, conversational English to produce working computer code. Demonstration participants, who included personnel from several offices within PAE Mission Systems, used modern agentic development tools to rapidly prototype and iterate on real-world Navy problem scenarios in a hands-on workshop environment. The demonstration showed what is capable with agentic coding tools and the value that they can bring to the development, security, and operations pipeline.

Guidance from the Department of War is clear: Organizations should leverage AI technologies to modernize software systems, enhance operational efficiency, and accelerate capability delivery. The Overmatch RCC is moving rapidly to meet that intent.

“We are working on integrating this capability enterprise-wide for our developers and sailors ashore,” said Brian Rose, assistant program manager, Overmatch Digital Infrastructure and Services section. “But what's really exciting is bringing vibe coding to the edge so even the most junior Sailors and Marines can fill in capability gaps in days instead of years while deployed.”

The artificial intelligence and coding agents shorten the time between identifying a requirement to fielding a solution. Results are now possible within days, or even minutes, rather than years, said Rose.

Additionally, the simplicity of the systems removes barriers for non-technical users to solve their individual problems without having to rely on professional developers. That frees up experienced personnel to focus on the really wicked problems, said Mike Lee, capability lead, Overmatch Digital Infrastructure and Services section. Leaders can use the vibe-coding tools to refine their own vision before communicating requirements to their team, added Lee.

Formerly known as Project Overmatch, the Overmatch Rapid Capability Cell delivers advanced prototype capabilities for PAE Mission Systems by partnering directly with the Fleet to meet the warfighter’s immediate operational needs.
items.titleZh: 西海岸“氛围”编程
items.summaryZh: 组合采办执行官（PAE）任务系统优势快速能力小组（RCC）于9月16日至17日在洛马角海军基地老城园区，为数十名信息技术专业人员和高级领导人举办了一场人工智能“氛围编程”（vibe coding）演示。该演示展示了智能体编码工具的能力，以及它们能为开发、安全和运营流水线带来的价值。
zhParas: 圣迭戈——9月16日至17日，组合采办执行官（PAE）任务系统优势快速能力小组（RCC）在洛马角海军基地老城园区，为数十名信息技术专业人员和高级领导人举办了一场人工智能“氛围编程”（vibe coding）演示。
氛围编程是指人类使用常规的对话式英语向人工智能代理发出提示，以生成可运行的计算机代码。演示参与者包括来自 PAE 任务系统内多个办公室的人员，他们在动手实践工作坊环境中使用现代代理式开发工具，对真实的海军问题场景进行快速原型设计和迭代。该演示展示了代理式编码工具的能力，以及它们能为开发、安全和运营流水线带来的价值。
战争部的指导意见很明确：各组织应利用人工智能技术来现代化软件系统、提升运营效率并加快能力交付。优势快速能力小组（Overmatch RCC）正在迅速行动以落实这一意图。
我们正致力于将这一能力在整个企业范围内整合，供我们的开发人员和岸上水兵使用，”优势数字基础设施与服务部门助理项目经理布赖恩·罗斯（Brian Rose）说。“但真正令人兴奋的是将氛围编程带到边缘，这样即使是最初级的水兵和海军陆战队员也能在部署期间用几天而不是几年的时间填补能力缺口。
罗斯说，人工智能和编码代理缩短了从确定需求到将解决方案投入使用之间的时间。现在，结果可在几天甚至几分钟内实现，而不是数年。
此外，这些系统的简便性消除了非技术用户解决自身问题的障碍，使他们无需依赖专业开发人员。优势数字基础设施与服务部门能力负责人迈克·李（Mike Lee）说，这使经验丰富的人员得以腾出精力，专注于真正棘手的问题。李补充说，领导者可以使用氛围编程工具，在向团队传达需求之前完善自己的构想。
Overmatch Rapid Capability Cell（超越快速能力小组）前身为 Project Overmatch（超越项目），它通过与舰队直接合作，为 PAE 任务系统交付先进原型能力，以满足作战人员的即时作战需求。

items.title: Connecting, Learning, and Elevating Defense Excellence!
items.author: David Carrera
items.summary: The Defense Service Office Symposium recently brought together defense practitioners, legal leaders, and dedicated professionals from across the country for an inspiring week focused on professional development, advocacy, and collaborative leadership. It was a forum to sharpen legal tradecraft, exchange insights, and address the evolving landscape of military justice. Highlights included: Insights
items.body: The Defense Service Office Symposium recently brought together defense practitioners, legal leaders, and dedicated professionals from across the country for an inspiring week focused on professional development, advocacy, and collaborative leadership. It was a forum to sharpen legal tradecraft, exchange insights, and address the evolving landscape of military justice. Highlights included: Insights from senior leadership — Judge Advocate General of the Navy Maj. Gen. David Bligh and Commander, Naval Legal Service Command Rear Adm. Dom Flatt. National expertise — guest speakers and legal mind leaders from across the nation delivered engaging sessions on advanced trial tactics, client advocacy, and effective leadership within the JAG Corps. Collaboration and mentorship — beyond the classroom, defense advocates had the opportunity to network, share best practices, and build stronger mentorship networks across military regions.

items.title: Florida Air Force Bases Evacuate Planes, Personnel as Hurricane Isaias Bears Down
items.author: Steve Losey
items.summary: The Air Force has begun evacuating stealth fighters, gunships, and special operations planes ahead of Hurricane Isaias expected landfall over the Gulf Coast this weekend. The post Florida Air Force Bases Evacuate Planes, Personnel as Hurricane Isaias Bears Down appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
Editor’s Note: This story was updated Oct. 9 with more information.

The Air Force has begun evacuating stealth fighters, gunships, and special operations planes ahead of Hurricane Isaias’ expected landfall over the Gulf Coast this weekend.

Severe storms can be devastating for Air Force bases, endangering lives, damaging aircraft and buildings, and battering runways.

As of Oct. 8, three bases in Florida and one in Mississippi have begun flying out F-35 Lightning IIs, AC-130J Ghostriders, MC-130J Commando IIs, and more

Tyndall Air Force Base, Fla.—which was ravaged by Hurricane Michael in 2018—began moving out aircraft Oct. 8 including F-35s from the 325th Fighter Wing, a base spokesman told Air & Space Forces Magazine. Some aircraft were in the air in the morning, the spokesperson said, but the situation remained “fluid,” and it was unclear how many would ultimately fly out. The wing declined to say where the planes were going, citing operational security concerns.

Isaias is currently gathering strength in the Gulf of Mexico, with maximum sustained winds increasing to nearly 120 miles per hour, the National Hurricane Center said the morning of Oct. 9. That qualifies as a Category 3 hurricane.

“Isaias is expected to be at or near major hurricane strength when it makes landfall” late Oct. 9, according to the latest National Hurricane Center advisory. Isaias is expected to hit the United States’ northern Gulf Coast and impact parts of Alabama, Georgia, and the Florida panhandle, which could also face tornadoes.

“Hurricane force winds are expected to spread inland as far as 100 miles from the coast,” according to the advisory, adding that the storm will also bring 4 to 8 inches of rain, though “localized totals up to 15 inches are possible” across the Florida panhandle and Big Bend.

Bases in the region are on guard. Tyndall moved to Hurricane Condition 2 status on Oct. 8, meaning destructive winds of 58 miles per hour or greater were possible over the next 24 hours. Tyndall also limited installation access to mission-essential personnel, residents, and other authorized personnel, and facilities such as child care centers, the fitness center, and the commissary began closing throughout Oct. 8.

Another Florida installation, Eglin Air Force Base, flew its airworthy aircraft—including planes assigned to the 96th Test Wing, 53rd Wing, and 33rd Fighter Wing—to safer locations on Oct. 8. Aircraft that could not fly were placed in hangars for protection.

Civilian authorities in the Eglin region have also ordered some residents to evacuate. Eglin commander Col. Chris Keithley issued his own limited evacuation order for service members, Pentagon employees, and dependents living in certain parts of Okaloosa County, Fla., authorizing them to be reimbursed for their evacuation travel and saying they are not to return until directed to do so.

Eglin’s 96th Medical Group Hospital and pharmacies closed, but emergency operations, labor and delivery, and inpatient services remain open, the base said.

“The safety of our Airmen, their families, and our community is our highest priority,” Keithley said in a statement. “As we prepare for the potential impacts of Hurricane Isaias, we are taking proactive steps to protect our people and aircraft entrusted to our care. Relocating our aircraft is a deliberate decision that reflects our responsibility to be good stewards of taxpayer resources while preserving our ability to execute the mission.”

The home of Air Force Special Operations Command, Hurlburt Field, Fla., moved to Hurricane Condition 3 on Oct. 7 and limited base access to mission-essential personnel.

A spokesperson for Hurlburt also told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the base’s 1st Special Operations Wing had started flying out its AC-130s and MC-130s to Little Rock Air Force Base, Arkansas.

The wing commander also ordered roughly 1,000 Hurlburt residents in privatized military housing to evacuate by 5 p.m. on Oct. 8. Hurlburt said it doesn’t expect the storm surge to reach or damage housing structures, but that rising water levels could inundate a critical station that would interrupt vital wastewater, sewage, and potable water services.

The 403rd Wing at Keesler Air Force Base, Mississippi, also moved their aircraft Oct. 8 as the hurricane approached. One of its units, the 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron better known as the Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunters, is continuing to fly recon missions into Isaias from Kelly Field in Texas. Those flights help provide data for the National Hurricane Center, which helps improve the center’s storm tracking and intensity forecasts.

Almost eight years ago, Tyndall was wrecked by Hurricane Michael when the Category 5 storm struck on Oct. 10, 2018. Aircraft that were not able to be flown out beforehand—including F-22 Raptor fighters—were damaged, some beyond repair, when their hangars were hit, and numerous buildings sustained damage that the Air Force called “catastrophic” at the time. Tyndall took years to recover, and its F-22 operations moved first to Eglin before ultimately settling at Joint Base Langley-Eustis, Va..

In March 2019, Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska experienced severe flooding, caused by the combination of a bomb cyclone’s violent weather and the melting of record snowfall. Those floods left dozens of buildings and much of Offutt’s flightline partially submerged, and prompted the base to evacuate several aircraft.

News Editor Greg Hadley contributed to this report.
items.titleZh: 佛罗里达空军基地在飓风“伊萨亚斯”逼近之际撤离飞机和人员
items.summaryZh: 美国空军已开始撤离隐身战斗机、炮艇机和特种作战飞机，以赶在飓风“伊萨亚斯”预计本周末在墨西哥湾沿岸登陆之前完成。《佛罗里达空军基地在飓风“伊萨亚斯”逼近之际撤离飞机和人员》一文首先发表于《空军与太空军杂志》。
zhParas: 编者注：本报道于10月9日更新，补充了更多信息。
空军已开始撤离隐身战斗机、炮艇机和特种作战飞机，以赶在飓风“伊萨亚斯”预计本周末在墨西哥湾沿岸登陆之前完成转移。
强风暴可能对空军基地造成毁灭性破坏，危及生命、损坏飞机和建筑，并重创跑道。
截至10月8日，佛罗里达州的三座基地和密西西比州的一座基地已开始将F-35“闪电II”、AC-130J“幽灵骑士”、MC-130J“突击队员II”等飞机转移出去。
一名基地发言人告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，佛罗里达州廷德尔空军基地——该基地曾在2018年遭飓风“迈克尔”重创——已于10月8日开始转移飞机，包括来自第325战斗机联队的F-35。该发言人说，部分飞机当天上午已经升空，但情况仍在“变化中”，尚不清楚最终将有多少架飞机飞离。该联队以作战安全关切为由，拒绝透露这些飞机的目的地。
美国国家飓风中心10月9日上午表示，伊萨亚斯目前正在墨西哥湾增强，最大持续风速已增至接近每小时120英里。这已达到三级飓风标准。
伊萨亚斯预计将于10月9日晚些时候登陆，届时强度将达到或接近强飓风级别，”根据国家飓风中心最新公告。伊萨亚斯预计将袭击美国墨西哥湾北部沿岸，并影响阿拉巴马州、佐治亚州和佛罗里达狭长地带的部分地区，这些地区还可能面临龙卷风。
公告称，“飓风级大风预计将从海岸向内陆延伸至多100英里”，并补充说风暴还将带来4至8英寸降雨，但佛罗里达狭长地带和大本德地区“局部总降雨量可能高达15英寸”。
该地区基地处于警戒状态。廷德尔于10月8日进入飓风二级戒备状态，这意味着未来24小时内可能出现每小时58英里或以上的破坏性大风。廷德尔还将基地准入限制为任务必需人员、居民及其他授权人员，儿童保育中心、健身中心和军人服务社等设施于10月8日全天陆续关闭。
佛罗里达州另一处基地——埃格林空军基地——于10月8日将其适航飞机飞往更安全地点，其中包括隶属于第96测试联队、第53联队和第33战斗机联队的飞机。无法飞行的飞机则被安置在机库中加以保护。
埃格林地区的民政当局也已下令部分居民撤离。埃格林指挥官克里斯·基思利上校针对居住在佛罗里达州奥卡卢萨县某些地区的军人、五角大楼雇员和家属发布了自己的有限撤离令，授权为其报销撤离差旅费用，并表示在接到指示前不得返回。
基地表示，埃格林第96医疗大队医院和药房已关闭，但急诊手术、分娩和住院服务仍保持开放。
我们的空军人员、他们的家人以及我们社区的安全是我们的最高优先事项，”基思利在一份声明中说。“在我们为飓风‘伊萨亚斯’可能造成的影响做准备时，我们正在采取积极措施，保护我们的人员和托付给我们照管的飞机。转移我们的飞机是一项深思熟虑的决定，体现了我们有责任妥善管理纳税人资源，同时保持执行任务的能力。
空军特种作战司令部所在地、佛罗里达州赫尔伯特机场于10月7日进入飓风三级戒备状态，并将基地准入限制为执行任务必需人员。
赫尔伯特的一位发言人也告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，该基地第1特种作战联队已开始将其AC-130和MC-130飞往阿肯色州小石城空军基地。
联队指挥官还命令约1000名居住在私有化军人住房中的赫尔伯特居民在10月8日下午5点前撤离。赫尔伯特表示，预计风暴潮不会到达或损坏住房结构，但水位上涨可能淹没一个关键站点，从而中断重要的废水、排污和饮用水服务。
密西西比州基斯勒空军基地的第403联队也于10月8日在飓风逼近时转移了飞机。其下属单位之一——第53气象侦察中队，更广为人知的名字是空军预备役“飓风猎人”——继续从得克萨斯州凯利机场飞入“伊萨亚斯”执行侦察任务。这些飞行有助于为国家飓风中心提供数据，从而帮助改进该中心的风暴路径追踪和强度预报。
将近八年前，2018年10月10日，5级飓风“迈克尔”来袭，廷德尔遭到重创。未能提前飞离的飞机——包括F-22“猛禽”战斗机——在机库遭袭时受损，其中一些无法修复；许多建筑也遭受了空军当时称之为“灾难性”的损坏。廷德尔花了数年时间才恢复，其F-22作战行动先是转移到埃格林空军基地，最终落户于弗吉尼亚州兰利-尤斯蒂斯联合基地。
2019年3月，内布拉斯加州奥福特空军基地遭遇严重洪水，原因是炸弹气旋的恶劣天气与创纪录降雪融化共同作用。洪水导致数十栋建筑和奥福特基地的大部分停机线被部分淹没，并促使该基地转移了数架飞机。
新闻编辑格雷格·哈德利对本报道有贡献。

Urgent Response 26 focused on emergency response procedures including enhanced force protection measures, counter sUAS procedures and trauma services, enhancing participants ability to identify, report and respond t
items.body: U.S. Marines and federal employees conduct a simulated urgent response to a small Unmanned Aircraft System (sUAS) at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, Oct. 8, 2026. Urgent Response 26 focused on emergency response procedures including enhanced force protection measures, counter sUAS procedures and trauma services, enhancing participants ability to identify, report and respond to potential threats on MCB Camp Lejeune and Marine Corps Air Station New River. items.titleZh: B-Roll：紧急响应26
items.summaryZh: 2026年10月8日，美国海军陆战队队员和联邦雇员在北卡罗来纳州海军陆战队基地（MCB）勒琼营对小型无人机系统（sUAS）进行模拟紧急响应。“紧急响应26”聚焦于应急响应程序，包括强化的部队防护措施、反小型无人机系统程序和创伤救治服务，提升参与者识别、报告和应对潜在威胁的能力。

items.title: US Army Corps of Engineers failed to explain drop in environmental mitigation work: Watchdog
items.author: Zita Fletcher
items.summary: A chart published by GAO shows a sharp decline in the agency's decisions to make mitigation plans for wildlife and habitat protection from 2022 to 2025.
items.body:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers did not seek to mitigate environmental damage for more than 50 projects over the past five years and did not provide detailed explanations to Congress, a government watchdog found.

Measures to prevent environmental damage were proposed in only 22 of 74 civil works projects the Corps submitted to Congress for approval from 2020 to 2025, according to a report published Wednesday by the Government Accountability Office.

The Corps deemed that no such measures were needed for the remaining 52 projects and failed to provide detailed evidence as to why, the watchdog alleges.

The agency regularly works to improve water navigation channels to prevent flooding and restore aquatic habitats around the country through its civil works program. It is required by statute to make detailed reports to Congress outlining whether its projects will require measures to prevent possible harm to fish, wildlife and the environment.

The engineers are expected “to plan for environmental mitigation — that is, to take actions to avoid, minimize, or compensate for expected losses to fish and wildlife and damage to ecological resources,” which could include reinforcing riverbanks or restoring wetland areas to create new habitats for fish and wildlife, according to the report.

The Corps of Engineers may decide not to undertake conservation measures if it deems certain projects will not cause harm. However, the Army is expected to provide Congress with clear explanations for those decisions.

A chart published by GAO shows a sharp decline in the Corps’ decisions to make mitigation plans for wildlife and habitat protection from 2022 to 2025. In 2024, for example, the agency decided that only one of 13 projects would require measures to safeguard the environment.

The GAO’s chart shows zero mitigation plans made in 2025.

In its findings, the GAO alleges that the Corps failed to provide necessary details to Congress demonstrating the reasons behind its decision-making in cases when it deemed no environmental protection measures were needed.

The watchdog said the vast majority of documents sent to Congress during those five years contained broad and general language that failed to clarify how the Corps reached its decisions.

The GAO recommended that the Army establish clear guidance for the Corps to document how it reaches decisions to keep Congress and the public better informed.

The Army disputed the GAO’s recommendations in a Sept. 16 letter signed by D. Lee Forsgren, the senior official performing the duties of the Army’s assistant secretary for civil works.

“We do not concur with the recommendation in the draft that we need to create more guidance about mitigation decision making on Civil Works projects,” Forsgren wrote.

“The water resources project reports (including associated Chief’s Reports) produced by USACE have sufficient technical information for decision makers and the public and resource agencies to understand when habitat mitigation is or is not included in a final recommendation.”

Zita Ballinger Fletcher previously served as editor of Military History Quarterly and Vietnam magazines and as the historian of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. She holds an M.A. with distinction in military history.
items.titleZh: 监督机构：美国陆军工程兵团未能解释环境缓解工作减少
items.summaryZh: 美国政府问责局发布的一张图表显示，从2022年到2025年，美国陆军工程兵团为保护野生动物和栖息地而制定缓解计划的决定急剧减少。
zhParas: 一家政府监督机构发现，美国陆军工程兵团在过去五年中未为50多个项目寻求减轻环境损害，也未向国会提供详细解释。
美国政府问责局周三发布的一份报告显示，2020年至2025年，工程兵团提交国会审批的74个民用工程项目中，仅22个提出了防止环境损害的措施。
该监督机构指称，工程兵团认为其余52个项目无需此类措施，但未能提供详细证据说明原因。
该机构经常通过其民用工程项目改善通航水道以防洪，并恢复全国各地的水生栖息地。法律要求其向国会提交详细报告，说明其项目是否需要采取措施，以防止对鱼类、野生动物和环境造成可能损害。
报告称，工程兵团应“规划环境缓解措施——即采取行动，避免、尽量减少或补偿对鱼类和野生动物的预期损失以及对生态资源的损害”，这可能包括加固河岸或恢复湿地区域，为鱼类和野生动物创造新的栖息地。
如果工程兵团认为某些项目不会造成损害，它可以决定不采取保护措施。但是，美国陆军应就这些决定向国会提供明确解释。
美国政府问责局发布的一张图表显示，从2022年到2025年，陆军工程兵团为保护野生动物和栖息地制定缓解计划的决定急剧减少。例如，2024年，该机构认定13个项目中只有一个需要采取保护环境的措施。
美国政府问责局的图表显示，2025年制定的缓解计划为零。
在其调查结果中，美国政府问责局指称，陆军工程兵团未能向国会提供必要细节，以说明其在认为无需采取环境保护措施的情况下的决策理由。
该监督机构表示，这五年间送交国会的绝大多数文件包含宽泛笼统的措辞，未能说明陆军工程兵团是如何作出决策的。
美国政府问责局建议陆军为陆军工程兵团制定明确指南，要求其记录如何作出决策，以便让国会和公众更好地了解情况。
陆军在9月16日由D. Lee Forsgren签署的一封信中对美国政府问责局的建议提出异议。Forsgren是代行陆军负责土木工程的助理部长职责的高级官员。
我们不认同草案中的建议，即我们需要就民用工程项目的缓解决策制定更多指南，”福斯格伦写道。
美国陆军工程兵团（USACE）编制的水资源项目报告（包括相关的《工程兵司令报告》）包含足够的技术信息，使决策者、公众和资源机构能够了解最终建议中何时纳入或不纳入栖息地缓解措施。
齐塔·巴林杰·弗莱彻（Zita Ballinger Fletcher）曾任《军事历史季刊》和《越南》杂志编辑，并曾担任美国缉毒局历史学家。她以优异成绩获得军事历史学硕士学位。

items.title: In the Line of Care: Behind the lens – a corpsman in the Dragon’s Den
items.author: André B. Sobocinski, Historian
items.summary: In this edition of In the Line of Care, we spotlight an oral history excerpt with a CASEVAC hospital corpsman who served in Vietnam,
items.body:
There is a photograph in the Bureau of Medicine and Surgery (BUMED) historical archives of a young corpsman named “HM3 Levitt” hydrating a casualty with intravenous dextrose. The photo is captioned “CASEVAC corpsman on evacuation flight to a field hospital at Phu Bai, Vietnam in 1966.” Over the years the picture has proven to be extremely popular and widely used in articles, books and exhibits as a means of telling the story of the war and depicting the vital role of corpsmen like Levitt who flew casualty evacuations. The backstory of this young corpsman had been wholly unknown to us here at BUMED until a chance phone call in 2016 from a retired corpsman who knew the subject in the photograph: Ira Leslie Levitt (1) that led to an opportunity to speak with him.

Some five decades after the photograph had been taken, the memories of the war were still fresh – even raw – for Levitt. Like many who enlisted in 1963, Vietnam had not been in his vocabulary, but like most veterans of the war that experience the frontlines would prove life changing. The following is an excerpt from this oral history detailing the story behind this photograph.

“We landed in Da Nang at daybreak, and they dropped the ramp and told us to roll out on the tarmac. Everyone that was already there was laughing at us. There are ’Red Horses’ (2) on the tarmac. I thought to myself, ‘What are we doing here?’ They loaded us up on these big 8- and 12-wheelers and took us across the Da Nang River to Marble Mountain (3) where the helicopter squadrons were.

Aboard the choppers, we had dextrose and water and our first-aid kits. We could do almost anything. We weren’t supposed to start blood transfusions, but we did. And we improvised sometimes. When we didn’t have a scalpel, we would cut the sheath for a hypodermic needle on an angle so that it had a sharp point. If there was a wounded guy who wasn’t getting any air, we would slam it down in his cricoids, right at the Adam’s apple where there’s a soft spot. (4) I’d wrap his neck with a piece of gauze, and now he’s breathing and he’s got an IV.

My responsibility was to keep them alive until I got them to the field medical aid station and the field ambulance. There were a couple times that we were close enough to the Station Hospital in Da Nang that we could take them down there. (5)

I was in Marble Mountain for maybe four or five months, and then I went to Phu Bai, (6) which was about ten kilometers south of the old Imperial City of Hue. That’s where I spent most of my time and that’s where that photograph was taken.

I was 22 years old at the time, and I thought I was already a man. I was serving with kids 17 and 18 years old; these same kids were coming back to us with mortal wounds. One day I threw a poncho out of the helicopter after we evacuated a patient, and in the poncho was a leg. That really set me off for a while.

I didn’t lose many, and I think the guy in that picture of me holding the bottle of dextrose and water made it. I first saw that photograph three years ago and that brought it all home. I had never seen that picture before, but that’s what it was like all the time. Every day that I was on the job it was like that. We’d take fire every day.

We’d hear, ‘WIA [wounded in action], three down, coordinates XX.’ We’d fly over to those coordinates, and we’d say ‘Pop Smoke.’ (7) We’d identify the color for verification, because in the beginning, you might land in the wrong place in the middle of the night and they’d be shooting at you. We came back one time and there were a hundred holes in the bird, but not one of us got hit. That’s when you realize there’s a power bigger than us, right?

As I look back today, I thank G-D I'm still alive, however the memories never go away.”

The Navy Medicine Oral History Project was started in the 1980s as a means of capturing the stories and important experiences of the men and women of Navy Medicine, both past and present. Future installments of the “In the Line of Care” series will feature some of these stories captured over the years.

Levitt, Leslie I. Oral History, April 26, 2016 (Conducted by A.B. Sobocinski). BUMED Oral History Collection.

(1) In 1965, Levitt served as a general duty corpsman aboard the hospital ship/station hospital USS Haven (AH-12) then moored in Long Beach and went through Field Medical Training at Camp Pendleton before being assigned to First Marine Aircraft Wing in Iwakuni and then to Marine Medium Helicopter Squadron (HMM) 163 in Okinawa. When he deployed to Vietnam in October 1965 he was assigned to HMM-161 in Da Nang. In January 1966, HMM-161 returned to Okinawa, and HMM-163 took its place in Vietnam, whereupon Levitt was reassigned back to HMM-163, and would remain with HMM-163 through December 1966. He was released from active duty in January 1967. (2) In 1956, the Air Force developed the Rapid Engineer Deployable Heavy Operation Repair Squadron (the Red Horse Squadrons). The first such unit, the 554th Civil Engineer Squadron (Heavy Lift) was deployed to Vietnam in October 1965. (3) Cluster of five marble and limestone hills located south of Da Nang. The five hills are named after the five elements: Kim (metal), Thuy (water), Moc (wood), Hoa (fire) and Tho (earth). During the Vietnam War it was home to the Marble Mountain Air Facility (MMAF) used by various U.S. Marine Corps squadrons. (4) An incision through the cricoid cartilages in the neck in order to a pass a tube as an emergency airway (cricothyrectomy). (5) Naval Station Hospital Da Nang. The hospital was located five miles north of the Marble Mountain Air Facility and was thirty miles from the DMZ. It was in operation from 1966 to 1970 as part of the Naval Support Activity Da Nang, which at the height of the Vietnam War was the Navy’s largest overseas shore command. Established in 1966, the hospital had an initial fifty bed capacity, that increased to 700 beds by 1968. Andrew, Jr., “For the Wounded a Place of Hope,” Stars and Stripes, 5 June 1968. (6) Phu Bai Combat Base (Phu Bai Airfield), Army/Marine base seven miles southeast of Hue, 1963-1975; home of the Naval Activity, Phu Bai. (7) During the Vietnam War, helicopter crews were able to locate their fellow Marines on the ground by asking them to "pop smoke in the landing zone.” The brightly colored smoke grenade identified the ground unit location, and provided landing zone wind information to the pilot. (Source: USMC Combat Helicopter Association, http://www.popasmoke.com).
items.titleZh: 在护理一线：镜头背后——龙穴中的医务兵
items.summaryZh: 在本期《在护理一线》中，我们聚焦一位曾在越南服役的伤员后送（CASEVAC）医务兵的口述历史节选，
zhParas: 美国海军医学与外科学局（BUMED）历史档案中有一张照片，照片上是一位名叫“HM3莱维特”的年轻医务兵，正用静脉注射葡萄糖为一名伤员补液。照片说明写着：“1966年，在越南富牌，伤员后送（CASEVAC）医务兵在飞往后送野战医院的航班上。”多年来，这张照片极受欢迎，被广泛用于文章、书籍和展览，以讲述这场战争的故事，并展现像莱维特这样执行伤员后送飞行任务的医务兵所发挥的关键作用。我们BUMED这里此前完全不知道这位年轻医务兵的身世背景，直到2016年一位认识照片中人物的退役医务兵偶然打来电话：伊拉·莱斯利·莱维特（1），这才让我们有机会与他交谈。
照片拍摄约五十年后，对莱维特来说，战争的记忆依然清晰——甚至仍然刺痛。像许多1963年入伍的人一样，越南当时并不在他的词汇里，但像这场战争的大多数老兵一样，亲历前线将被证明是改变一生的经历。以下是这段口述历史的节选，详述这张照片背后的故事。
我们在拂晓时抵达岘港，他们放下坡道，叫我们走到停机坪上。已经在那里的所有人都在嘲笑我们。停机坪上有‘红马’（2）。我心里想，‘我们到底在这里做什么？’他们让我们坐上这些八轮和十二轮大车，带我们穿过岘港河，来到直升机中队驻扎的大理石山（3）。
在直升机上，我们有葡萄糖、水和急救包。我们几乎什么都能做。我们本不该开始输血，但我们还是做了。有时我们还临时想办法。没有手术刀时，我们会把皮下注射针的护套斜着剪开，让它有一个尖头。如果有伤员喘不上气，我们就把针管猛地扎进他的环状软骨，正好在喉结那个柔软的地方。（4）我会用一块纱布缠住他的脖子，现在他呼吸了，也输上液了。
我的职责是让他们活着，直到我把他们送到野战医疗救护站和野战救护车。有几次我们离岘港的基地医院足够近，可以把他们送到那里。（5）
我在大理石山待了大概四五个月，然后去了富牌（6），那里位于顺化古皇城以南约十公里。我大部分时间都在那里度过，那张照片也是在那里拍摄的。
当时我22岁，以为自己已经是个男人了。我和一些17岁、18岁的孩子一起服役；正是这些孩子带着致命伤回到我们身边。有一天，我们后送一名伤员后，我把一件雨披从直升机上扔了出去，雨披里有一条腿。那件事让我有好一阵子都情绪失控。
我没失去多少人，我想那张我拿着葡萄糖和水的瓶子、照片里的那个家伙活了下来。我第一次看到那张照片是在三年前，那让我真切地体会到这一切。我以前从未见过那张照片，但当时情况一直就是那样。我执行任务期间的每一天都是那样。我们每天都遭到射击。
我们会听到：“WIA（战斗中负伤），三人倒下，坐标XX。”我们会飞到那些坐标处，然后喊“放烟”。我们会确认烟雾颜色以进行核实，因为一开始，你可能在半夜降错地方，而他们会朝你开枪。有一次我们回来，直升机上有一百个弹孔，但我们没有一个人被打中。就是那时你会意识到，有一种比我们更强大的力量，对吧？
今天回想起来，我感谢上帝我还活着，但那些记忆永远不会消失。
海军医学口述历史项目始于20世纪80年代，旨在记录海军医疗界男男女女——无论过去还是现在——的故事和重要经历。“In the Line of Care”系列未来的几期将呈现这些年来记录的其中一些故事。
莱维特，莱斯利·I. 口述历史，2016年4月26日（由A.B.索博辛斯基主持）。BUMED口述历史收藏。

(1) 1965年，莱维特在“黑文”号医院船/基地医院（USS Haven，AH-12）上担任一般勤务卫生兵，该船当时停泊在长滩；随后他在彭德尔顿营接受了战地医疗训练，之后被分配到岩国的海军陆战队第1航空联队，随后又被分配到冲绳的海军陆战队中型直升机中队（HMM）163。1965年10月部署到越南时，他被分配到岘港的HMM-161。1966年1月，HMM-161返回冲绳，HMM-163接替其进驻越南，莱维特随即被重新调回HMM-163，并一直留在HMM-163至1966年12月。1967年1月，他退出现役。 (2) 1956年，美国空军组建了快速工程部署重型作业修理中队（即“红马”中队）。首个此类单位——第554土木工程中队（重型起重）于1965年10月部署到越南。 (3) 位于岘港以南的五座大理石和石灰岩山丘群。这五座山以五行命名：Kim（金/金属）、Thuy（水）、Moc（木）、Hoa（火）和 Tho（土）。越南战争期间，这里是多支美国海军陆战队中队使用的“大理石山航空设施”（MMAF）所在地。 (4) 在颈部环状软骨处切开，以便置入导管作为紧急气道（环状软骨切开术）。 (5) 岘港海军基地医院。该医院位于大理石山航空设施以北五英里，距非军事区（DMZ）三十英里。它于1966年至1970年间运作，隶属于岘港海军支援活动部；在越南战争高峰时期，该部是海军最大的海外岸上司令部。医院成立于1966年，最初有50张床位，到1968年增至700张床位。小安德鲁，《为伤员提供希望之地》，《星条旗报》，1968年6月5日。 (6) 富牌战斗基地（富牌机场），位于顺化东南七英里的陆军/海军陆战队基地，1963—1975年；海军富牌活动部所在地。 (7) 越南战争期间，直升机机组人员能够通过要求地面上的海军陆战队战友“在着陆区发烟”来定位他们。颜色鲜艳的发烟手榴弹标明了地面部队位置，并向飞行员提供了着陆区风况信息。（来源：美国海军陆战队战斗直升机协会，http://www.popasmoke.com）。
items.zhFull:
美国海军医学与外科学局（BUMED）历史档案中有一张照片，照片上是一位名叫“HM3莱维特”的年轻医务兵，正用静脉注射葡萄糖为一名伤员补液。照片说明写着：“1966年，在越南富牌，伤员后送（CASEVAC）医务兵在飞往后送野战医院的航班上。”多年来，这张照片极受欢迎，被广泛用于文章、书籍和展览，以讲述这场战争的故事，并展现像莱维特这样执行伤员后送飞行任务的医务兵所发挥的关键作用。我们BUMED这里此前完全不知道这位年轻医务兵的身世背景，直到2016年一位认识照片中人物的退役医务兵偶然打来电话：伊拉·莱斯利·莱维特（1），这才让我们有机会与他交谈。

照片拍摄约五十年后，对莱维特来说，战争的记忆依然清晰——甚至仍然刺痛。像许多1963年入伍的人一样，越南当时并不在他的词汇里，但像这场战争的大多数老兵一样，亲历前线将被证明是改变一生的经历。以下是这段口述历史的节选，详述这张照片背后的故事。

我们在拂晓时抵达岘港，他们放下坡道，叫我们走到停机坪上。已经在那里的所有人都在嘲笑我们。停机坪上有‘红马’（2）。我心里想，‘我们到底在这里做什么？’他们让我们坐上这些八轮和十二轮大车，带我们穿过岘港河，来到直升机中队驻扎的大理石山（3）。

在直升机上，我们有葡萄糖、水和急救包。我们几乎什么都能做。我们本不该开始输血，但我们还是做了。有时我们还临时想办法。没有手术刀时，我们会把皮下注射针的护套斜着剪开，让它有一个尖头。如果有伤员喘不上气，我们就把针管猛地扎进他的环状软骨，正好在喉结那个柔软的地方。（4）我会用一块纱布缠住他的脖子，现在他呼吸了，也输上液了。

我的职责是让他们活着，直到我把他们送到野战医疗救护站和野战救护车。有几次我们离岘港的基地医院足够近，可以把他们送到那里。（5）

我在大理石山待了大概四五个月，然后去了富牌（6），那里位于顺化古皇城以南约十公里。我大部分时间都在那里度过，那张照片也是在那里拍摄的。

当时我22岁，以为自己已经是个男人了。我和一些17岁、18岁的孩子一起服役；正是这些孩子带着致命伤回到我们身边。有一天，我们后送一名伤员后，我把一件雨披从直升机上扔了出去，雨披里有一条腿。那件事让我有好一阵子都情绪失控。

我没失去多少人，我想那张我拿着葡萄糖和水的瓶子、照片里的那个家伙活了下来。我第一次看到那张照片是在三年前，那让我真切地体会到这一切。我以前从未见过那张照片，但当时情况一直就是那样。我执行任务期间的每一天都是那样。我们每天都遭到射击。

我们会听到：“WIA（战斗中负伤），三人倒下，坐标XX。”我们会飞到那些坐标处，然后喊“放烟”。我们会确认烟雾颜色以进行核实，因为一开始，你可能在半夜降错地方，而他们会朝你开枪。有一次我们回来，直升机上有一百个弹孔，但我们没有一个人被打中。就是那时你会意识到，有一种比我们更强大的力量，对吧？

今天回想起来，我感谢上帝我还活着，但那些记忆永远不会消失。

海军医学口述历史项目始于20世纪80年代，旨在记录海军医疗界男男女女——无论过去还是现在——的故事和重要经历。“In the Line of Care”系列未来的几期将呈现这些年来记录的其中一些故事。

莱维特，莱斯利·I. 口述历史，2016年4月26日（由A.B.索博辛斯基主持）。BUMED口述历史收藏。

items.title: 100 new UK jobs created as Kuwait buys British-made AI-enabled air defence systems
items.summary: British jobs and skills will be boosted by a £370 million deal as Kuwait buys vital air defence systems from a UK-based business.
items.body:
£370 million deal to strengthen Kuwait’s defences will create 100 UK jobs.

British-built air defence systems to protect the Gulf state.

Deal delivers on UK promise to back Gulf allies against regional threats.

The contract with MARSS Systems Limited, an EOS company, will create 100 new jobs in the UK, supporting skilled engineering and manufacturing roles.

MARSS will provide and integrate an advanced air defence system for Kuwait, incorporating jammers, radars and interceptors with its NiDAR platform, an AI-enabled command and control centre, to enhance the country’s ability to detect, deter and defeat airborne threats.

The deal is set to expand MARSS’s offices in the UK, with production based in Bristol, demonstrating how defence investment can deliver good growth in every postcode by creating jobs and opportunity across the UK.

The deal forms part of the UK’s Taskforce Sabre, which brings together government and industry to help Gulf states rapidly secure the systems and weapons they need. This follows Iran’s aggressive missile and drone attacks in the region.

Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, Luke Pollard MP, said:

This deal is a clear demonstration of the UK delivering on its promise to support our regional partners. By backing Kuwait with world-leading British technology, we’re not just strengthening a vital ally’s defences against real and growing threats. We’re creating skilled jobs here at home and proving that UK industry can deliver when it matters most.

Countering drones and aerial threats is not about any single system, it is about an intelligent, layered architecture that detects, decides and defeats within seconds, and MARSS has built exactly that. Through 2027, MARSS will integrate the sensors and effectors that protect Kuwait’s people, critical infrastructure and national assets, backed by British engineering and new skilled jobs here in the UK.

Countering drones and aerial threats is not about any single system, it is about an intelligent, layered architecture that detects, decides and defeats within seconds, and MARSS has built exactly that.

Through 2027, MARSS will integrate the sensors and effectors that protect Kuwait’s people, critical infrastructure and national assets, backed by British engineering and new skilled jobs here in the UK.

This latest deal builds on existing support, cementing the UK’s role as a trusted defence partner to Kuwait and the wider Gulf region.
items.titleZh: 科威特购买英国制造的人工智能防空系统，为英国创造100个新工作岗位
items.summaryZh: 科威特从一家英国企业购买关键防空系统，这笔3.7亿英镑的交易将促进英国的就业和技能发展。
zhParas: 价值3.7亿英镑的协议将加强科威特的防务，并创造100个英国工作岗位。
英国制造的防空系统将保护这个海湾国家。
该协议兑现了英国支持海湾盟友应对地区威胁的承诺。
与EOS旗下公司MARSS Systems Limited签订的合同将在英国创造100个新工作岗位，支持技能型工程和制造岗位。
MARSS将为科威特提供并整合一套先进防空系统，将其NiDAR平台——一个人工智能赋能的指挥控制中心——与干扰机、雷达和拦截弹相结合，以增强该国探测、威慑和击败空中威胁的能力。
该协议将扩大MARSS在英国的办公机构，生产基地位于布里斯托尔，表明国防投资如何通过在全英创造就业和机会，为每个地区带来良好增长。
这项协议是英国“佩剑”特别工作组的一部分，该工作组汇集政府与产业界，帮助海湾国家迅速获得其所需的系统和武器。此前，伊朗在该地区发动了咄咄逼人的导弹和无人机袭击。
国防战备与工业大臣、议会下院议员卢克·波拉德表示：
这项协议清楚地表明，英国正在履行其支持地区伙伴的承诺。通过以世界领先的英国技术支持科威特，我们不仅是在加强一个重要盟友抵御真实且不断增长威胁的防御能力。我们还在国内创造技能型就业岗位，并证明英国工业能够在最关键的时刻交付。
这项协议清楚地表明，英国正在履行其支持地区伙伴的承诺。
通过以世界领先的英国技术支持科威特，我们不仅是在加强一个重要盟友抵御真实且不断增长威胁的防御能力。我们还在国内创造技能型就业岗位，并证明英国工业能够在最关键的时刻交付。
MARSS公司首席执行官约翰内斯·平尔表示：
反制无人机和空中威胁并不取决于任何单一系统，而取决于一个能够在数秒内探测、决策并挫败威胁的智能分层架构，而MARSS正是打造了这样的架构。到2027年，MARSS将整合用于保护科威特人民、关键基础设施和国家资产的传感器与效应器，并以英国工程技术以及在英国本土新增的熟练技术岗位为支撑。
反制无人机和空中威胁并不取决于任何单一系统，而取决于一个能够在数秒内探测、决策并挫败威胁的智能分层架构，而MARSS正是打造了这样的架构。
到2027年，MARSS将整合用于保护科威特人民、关键基础设施和国家资产的传感器与效应器，并以英国工程技术以及在英国本土新增的熟练技术岗位为支撑。
英国已通过 Rapid Sentry 陆基防空导弹系统支持科威特。英国皇家空军的ORCUS系统也正在该国运行，帮助人员及早探测无人机并采取果断行动。
这项最新协议以现有支持为基础，巩固了英国作为科威特及更广泛海湾地区可信赖防务伙伴的角色。
